title: Runtime and CLI Reference
text: Runtime and CLI Reference How AIWAF works: system architecture AIWAF exposes language-specific middleware, engine, and CLI APIs. There is no shared /api/v1 bearer-token management service in the current repo. Python # Bare help selects the single installed framework aiwaf --help # Explicit Flask policy commands aiwaf flask blocklist migrate aiwaf flask status # Django management commands python manage.py detect_and_train python manage.py regenerate_model python manage.py aiwaf_reset --keywords --confirm python manage.py aiwaf_logging --status python manage.py geo_block_country list # Explicit adapter dispatch aiwaf django aiwaf_list --all aiwaf flask --help aiwaf fastapi --help Bare Python commands detect the single installed framework. With multiple frameworks, use the explicit prefixes above. Django keeps management-command names, and fast is an alias for fastapi . Use --framework and --app with aiwaf init for route discovery; FastAPI training separately uses --app . Node.js cd js AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG=/path/to/access.log npm run train npm run aiwaf -- status npm run aiwaf -- list blocklist npm run aiwaf -- add blocklist 203.0.113.9 "manual block" npm run aiwaf -- add ip-exemption 203.0.113.10 "trusted monitor" npm run aiwaf -- geo summary npm run aiwaf -- model info npm run aiwaf -- export aiwaf-export.json Use Redis or another shared cache for consistent rate limiting across multiple Node processes. Without shared state, the in-memory fallback is process-local. In an application with the npm package installed, use npx aiwaf --help ; the source commands above run from js/ . These Node CLI commands operate on legacy stores. The explicit native engine has dedicated event files and model snapshots; its state is not managed or imported automatically by the legacy CLI. See native operations . Java aiwaf-cli status aiwaf-cli diagnose --model model.json aiwaf-cli blocked aiwaf-cli unblock 203.0.113.10 aiwaf-cli train --events events.json --out model.json --backend java aiwaf-cli model status --path model.json Adapter and binding references Python adapters Node.js entry points Java engine Rust/Python and WASM functions Website endpoints This Flask documentation application defines its own /health , /aiwaf/status , /aiwaf/allowlist , /aiwaf/blocklist , and /aiwaf/keywords routes. Those are website-specific handlers, not a portable AIWAF API. Their implementation does not provide the bearer-token authentication previously described here.

title: How AIWAF Works
text: How AIWAF Works AIWAF sits inside the application request lifecycle. Framework adapters turn live HTTP requests into policy inputs, deterministic controls make immediate decisions, and optional anomaly models add evidence from recent behavior. On this page Two connected execution paths Responsibilities of each layer How route policies become decisions A block is a decision; a blocklist is state State ownership explains multi-worker behavior How anomaly detection contributes The learning loop What happens after the handler Read the runtime internals Two connected execution paths The system has a request path for enforcing the current policy and a learning path for improving future decisions. Configuration, route metadata, runtime stores, and model artifacts connect them. Framework adapter Extract method, path, headers, client address, and available handler metadata. Policy and checks Select applicable protections, read state, and return an early denial when a check fails. Application handler Allowed requests reach the normal application code. Response observations Record status, duration, and behavior; response-aware adapters may make another decision. This is a conceptual flow, not a universal middleware ordering. Python wrappers, Node middleware, and Java filters attach to different framework hooks. The runtime-specific pages below explain the actual execution boundaries. Responsibilities of each layer Layer Responsibility Example Adapter Read framework request/response data and intercept execution. Django middleware, Express middleware, Spring filter. Policy planner Combine enabled middleware with route metadata and path rules. A webhook may run header checks without form timing. Deterministic checks Enforce concrete limits and matching rules. A rate window over its configured maximum returns a denial. Behavior model Score a feature vector using a trained forest. Repeated unknown-route probes can add anomaly evidence. Runtime state Remember recent activity, exemptions, blocks, and learned keywords. A later request observes an active IP block. Learning pipeline Build future models and keyword state from recorded traffic. A scheduled job trains from access logs. How route policies become decisions A manifest records discovered routes, methods, and inferred handler intent. Source analysis can supply signals such as JSON responses, form handling, or authentication calls when framework metadata is incomplete. The manifest compiler translates those signals into middleware disablement and rate-limit overrides. The runtime combines those generated rules with explicitly configured path policies and decorator or annotation metadata. A protection runs only when it is enabled and applicable under that runtime's policy rules. An auto selection starts from the canonical set and omits checks unsupported by detected application signals; it is not itself an anomaly detector. For example, an API endpoint may omit HTML form timing while keeping headers and rate limits. A login form needs different checks. Keep inferred policies reviewable: a route name or return type is evidence about intent, not proof of authorization. A block is a decision; a blocklist is state A failing header, method, or rate check can reject the current request. Some checks also record an offense or create a temporary IP block. Those are separate effects: returning a denial does not imply that every later request is permanently blocked. Reputation handling records weighted offenses and can escalate temporary block durations. Later requests consult block expiry and exemption rules. Which checks mutate reputation and which response statuses they return are runtime-specific. State ownership explains multi-worker behavior State category Typical contents Architectural consequence Recent enforcement state Rate buckets, form timestamps, UUID scores, recent request history. Independent worker memory creates independent windows and counts. Operational stores Blocklists, exemptions, geo policy, learned keywords. Persistence across restarts is different from consistent access across processes. Model artifacts Forest state, feature schema, training metadata. Loading the same artifact does not share rate-limit or blocklist state. A local file can persist data while leaving other request counters process-local. Choose sharing separately for every state category. Java's Redis backend shares enforcement state atomically; Node rate limiting accepts a shared cache; Python sharing depends on the adapter and its configured stores. How anomaly detection contributes An Isolation Forest repeatedly partitions feature samples using random feature choices and split points. Samples isolated in fewer splits tend to receive more anomalous scores. The forest learns a distribution of request behavior; it does not identify a vulnerability or understand the application's authorization rules. The host runtime decides whether a score is enough to block. Model availability, training volume, thresholds, route eligibility, and recent-behavior confirmation can all affect that decision. For example, Node's unknown-route path requires both a sufficiently trained model and scanning-related behavior before issuing an anomaly block. Feature What it describes Why it helps path_len Length of the request path. Unusually long probing paths. kw_hits Matches against malicious keywords. Known probing patterns within a path. resp_time Response duration in seconds. Behavior that differs from the normal timing distribution. status_idx An encoded response-status category. Response outcomes without treating status codes as continuous measurements. burst_count Requests associated with the client in the burst window. Rapid repeated activity. total_404 Not-found responses in the relevant per-client history. Repeated discovery of nonexistent routes. The feature order is part of the model contract. A trainer and scorer must agree on the order, status mapping, time units, and window semantics. Summary fields ending in _ms use milliseconds; the feature vector uses seconds. Sharing feature names alone does not make every model artifact interchangeable. The learning loop Request logs Completed responses supply paths, client identity, status, and timing. Feature extraction Records are normalized and combined with per-client activity windows. Train and review Volume thresholds gate model training; route exemptions filter learned keywords. Publish artifacts The runtime loads persisted model state and updated learned keywords. The training job is separate from ordinary application request handling. Reading logs and rebuilding a forest does not need to happen for every request. Runtime keyword learning, where enabled, is a separate mechanism that can use completed-response signals. Current Python model persistence uses JSON rather than executable Python-object serialization. Java can exchange the Python Rust-model forest state for the supported schema. JavaScript-native artifacts and legacy formats require their own compatibility checks. What happens after the handler Response observations make real status and duration available. This matters for distinguishing a normal request from repeated 404 probing. A response-aware integration may evaluate behavior after the handler returns, but a response already committed or streamed to the client cannot be replaced. Java's Spring filter explicitly distinguishes an uncommitted synchronous response from committed or asynchronous output. Other adapters use their framework's hooks for logging and learning. Avoid assuming that post-response scoring can prevent every byte from leaving the application. Read the runtime internals Python: shared core, framework hooks, policy and training Node.js: middleware order, denial paths and finish hooks Java: engine decisions, Spring discovery and distributed state Rust/WASM: host bindings, matchers and forest implementation Python native request engine Release candidate: this page documents Python 1.1.8 and Rust/Python 0.2.7 in the current source checkout. Source versions do not establish registry availability. Python 1.1.8 requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.7 ; framework dependencies remain extras. Rust owns the native CSV pipeline configuration, enforcement order, SQL and keyword inspection, geo/blocklist decisions, rate buckets, form timing, UUID scores, anomaly history/inference, keyword learning, and CSV logging. Python supplies framework routes, authentication facts, GeoIP lookup, bounded request buffering, and response construction. Training and management still have Python interfaces. Install the explicit native adapter instead of the existing AIWAF middleware chain. Installing the required Rust dependency does not automatically switch existing applications to this pipeline. Legacy adapters remain available for custom stores and hooks; their configuration and fallback behavior are separate. Two engine calls surround application execution: begin enforces request checks; finish observes the response and writes state/logs. Java remains native Java; Node/WASM does not expose Python filesystem CSV bindings. Continue with the request lifecycle , the native profile , migration , and performance and deployment .

title: Configuration Reference
text: Configuration Reference Configuration is adapter-specific. Use the names accepted by your runtime, and apply settings before registering protection. The tables below describe source defaults; they do not guarantee that a middleware is selected or that a route is protected. Inputs and precedence | Policy and exemptions | Workers and shared state | Default tables Inputs and precedence Runtime Input Resolution Flask Flat app.config['AIWAF_*'] settings; constructor middleware selection Load application configuration before AIWAF(app) . A shell variable does not automatically become Flask app.config. The middleware reads adapter settings and its own defaults. Django Flat settings in settings.py Explicit flat settings take precedence over legacy AIWAF_SETTINGS compatibility mappings for settings that use set-if-missing. Django does not automatically read arbitrary environment variables; map them in settings.py. FastAPI Nested constructor options or AIWAFConfig Defaults, then JSON file, then recognized environment mappings, then explicit constructor overrides. If a config object is supplied, it is used directly rather than rebuilding from config_file/overrides. Node.js Options to the framework adapter The normalized resolver uses the first defined canonical option, supported aliases, legacy settings, recognized environment variables, and finally defaults. false and 0 remain explicit values. Java/Spring AiwafConfig , nested JSON, environment, Spring properties Spring's loader creates defaults/file configuration, applies supported environment mappings, then Spring property lookups. Custom configuration beans replace auto-configuration where supported. Rust/WASM Arguments to primitive bindings These bindings are not a framework configuration loader. Host adapters control middleware, policy, storage, and proxy handling. Flask and Django flat settings The nested Python table below is the shared configuration manager, primarily exposed through FastAPI. It is not the Flask/Django constructor signature. Their important flat names include AIWAF_RATE_WINDOW (seconds), AIWAF_RATE_MAX and AIWAF_RATE_FLOOD (integer counts), AIWAF_EXEMPT_PATHS (path list), AIWAF_PATH_RULES (rule list), AIWAF_GEO_BLOCK_COUNTRIES and AIWAF_GEO_ALLOW_COUNTRIES (country-code lists), and AIWAF_MODEL_PATH (path). Consult each adapter's settings guide for the full flat surface. # Flask: set values before middleware registration. app.config.update( AIWAF_RATE_WINDOW=10, AIWAF_RATE_MAX=20, AIWAF_RATE_FLOOD=40, AIWAF_RATE_CACHE_BACKEND='redis', AIWAF_REDIS_URL='redis://localhost:6379/0', AIWAF_RATE_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX='my-service:rate:', ) AIWAF(app, middlewares=['all']) Flask's rate middleware defaults to 10 seconds, 20 requests, and flood threshold 40. The website overrides these values in app.py. Node's normalized defaults are 60 seconds, 100 requests, and flood threshold 200. Do not use website thresholds as universal package defaults. FastAPI nested options from fastapi import FastAPI from aiwaf.fast import AIWAF app = FastAPI() AIWAF(app, middlewares=['all'], rate_limiting={'window_seconds': 10, 'max_requests': 20, 'flood_threshold': 40, 'cache_backend': 'redis', 'redis_url': 'redis://localhost:6379/0', 'cache_key_prefix': 'my-service:rate:'}) The shared environment loader recognizes names such as AIWAF_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS and AIWAF_RATE_MAX_REQUESTS . Those differ from the Flask/Django flat names. Boolean strings accept true , 1 , yes , and on as true; list mappings split comma-separated values. File lists use JSON arrays. Review the environment map before assuming a setting is supported. Middleware, route policy, and exemptions all selects the canonical middleware set. auto omits checks based on detected application signals. Explicitly disabled middleware and route exemptions can bypass checks even when their configuration says enabled. Regenerate route manifests after route changes and inspect the selected middleware at runtime. Default exemptions differ. Django includes administrative/login paths; Flask includes health, crawler, static and asset paths. Private-address behavior also differs from an explicit trusted-client allowlist. Review Python default exemption lists and the policy lifecycle before interpreting a successful local request as a public-client test. Configure forwarding-header handling with the actual deployment topology. Java exposes trustedProxyCidrs and maxForwardedForEntries . Python and Node extraction use adapter-specific rules; these Java options are not portable knobs. Have the outer proxy overwrite untrusted client forwarding headers, and compare observed client addresses with the intended public client. Multiple workers and storage Persistent blocklist files, model storage, logs, and rate counters have separate ownership. A CSV blocklist does not share every in-memory counter. Flask/FastAPI use separate rate-cache settings; install the Redis client required by the selected backend. Flask rejects invalid Redis configuration at initialization. Python rate-cache failures produce generic HTTP 503 responses, and FastAPI does not silently select a process-local cache. Verify repeated requests across workers and inspect backend diagnostics. Node accepts a shared cache implementation; its fallback is process-local. Java Redis shares enforcement state within storageKeyPrefix , supports standalone mode, and defaults to fail_closed . Use the same namespace only for intentionally shared policy/state, and review schema compatibility before mixed-version deployments. Source default tables The Python table includes every leaf returned by the shared manager. The Node table includes normalized options, not every raw option consumed by individual modules (for example cache/WASM settings). The Java table includes public AiwafConfig field initializers. Disabled middleware can leave a setting inactive. These tables are a source snapshot, not your effective live configuration. Java typed fields ; Spring properties ; Java environment mappings . Legacy adapter native CSV settings These uppercase settings apply to the retained legacy adapters. The explicit native pipeline uses a separate lowercase profile. Setting Default and scope AIWAF_USE_RUST , AIWAF_RUST_CSV Enabled by default for supported Flask/Django native CSV dispatch. Set either application setting to False to disable it. FastAPI training also honors these application options. AIWAF_RUST_CSV=false environment variable Disables shared native dispatch outside Flask/Django application contexts. Configured framework settings take precedence over this environment fallback. AIWAF_CSV_REQUEST_CACHE Flask defaults to True . Reuses exemptions within a request while rechecking file metadata/configuration; does not cache rate mutations or blocklist expiry decisions. AIWAF_CSV_LOG_FSYNC Flask CSV logging defaults to False . True synchronizes each row to disk. Changed policy-state writes still synchronize. AIWAF_RUST_ISO_DATES=1 Optional environment flag for native ISO timestamp parsing. Python's faster C ISO parser remains the default. AIWAF_RATE_CACHE_BACKEND='csv' Explicit Flask selection of persistent shared rate buckets. Memory remains the default. Requires native support; unavailable/disabled native support returns HTTP 503. AIWAF_RATE_CSV_PATH Optional Flask path; defaults to rate_buckets.csv under AIWAF_DATA_DIR . # Set before AIWAF(app). app.config.update(AIWAF_USE_CSV=True, AIWAF_USE_RUST=True, AIWAF_RUST_CSV=True, AIWAF_CSV_LOG_FSYNC=False) # Optional, costlier than process memory: shared CSV rate counters. app.config['AIWAF_RATE_CACHE_BACKEND'] = 'csv' CSV buckets trim the request window, consume a request, evaluate thresholds, and persist TTL under one native transaction. Rewriting and syncing on every request can cost more than Redis or memory. A CSV blocklist alone does not select this rate backend. Native pipeline profile (Python 1.1.8) Release candidate: this page documents Python 1.1.8 and Rust/Python 0.2.7 in the current source checkout. Source versions do not establish registry availability. Python 1.1.8 requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.7 ; framework dependencies remain extras. Pass a dedicated lowercase config dictionary in Flask/FastAPI, or use AIWAF_CSV_PIPELINE in Django. Existing uppercase settings, nested AIWAFConfig dictionaries, PATH_RULES, manifests and custom policy callbacks are not merged into this profile. Unknown keys fail initialization. The profile is immutable; construct a new engine and reload workers to change it. Legacy Rust-disable flags do not select a Python fallback for this engine. Profile key Default and meaning enabled All eight stage names; explicitly select a subset if needed data_dir aiwaf_data; native policy CSV directory exempt_paths / exempt_ips /health, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml; no IPs. Literal case-insensitive path prefixes sql_mode / max_bytes block / 65536 bytes; off supported, monitor rejected; bounded structured traversal learning / top_n true / 10; sorted stable presence-keyword subset geo_allow / geo_block Empty arrays plus stored blocked countries; unknown country allowed rate_backend / rate_key_mode memory / ip_path; csv shares buckets, ip aggregates paths; Redis rejected rate_window / rate_max / rate_flood 10 seconds / 20 / 40; throttle 429, flood 403 with blocklist persistence honeypot_backend Django defaults to django_cache via CACHES; other native adapters default to csv (shared/persistent). memory is per engine/worker and resets on restart. Django accepts honeypot_cache_alias (default: default) min_form_time / max_page_time / skip_authenticated 1.0 seconds / 240 seconds / true uuid_score_enabled / uuid_window / uuid_threshold true / 60 seconds / 5; malformed weight 5, not-found weight 1, success decay 2 required_headers / header_min_score HTTP_USER_AGENT and HTTP_ACCEPT / 3; empty required list retains safety caps anomaly_window 60 seconds; history and loaded model inference are native and per worker log_path / log_fsync data_dir/requests.csv / false; immediate append, optional per-row fsync config = { "data_dir": "aiwaf_data", "rate_backend": "memory", "honeypot_backend": "csv", "log_fsync": False, } Keep CSV honeypot timing when workers need shared persistent timestamps. Choose memory explicitly only when local timing and reset on restart fit the deployment. The full source profile also includes keyword vocabulary, blocklist behavior and UUID weights; see rust/src/csv_pipeline.rs . Continue with the request lifecycle , the native profile , migration , and performance and deployment . Node native pipeline profile Native mode: Node source candidate aiwaf 1.1.4 declares aiwaf-wasm ^0.2.4 . Explicit native registration validates NativeRequestPipeline at startup; missing or incompatible support is an error. There is no JavaScript policy fallback for this engine. Installing the dependency does not switch an existing legacy middleware chain. Adapter options: profile , dataDir , logPath , logFsync , persistBlocks , model , synchronous countryLookup / authenticated / routeExists , and onError . Unknown options fail startup. The profile is immutable and accepts lowercase keys only; reconstruct/reload to change it. Profile keys Defaults and meaning enabled All eight stages exempt_paths / exempt_ips /health, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml; empty IPs; literal case-insensitive prefixes sql_mode / max_bytes block / 65536; off supported, monitor rejected rate_window / rate_max / rate_flood / rate_key_mode 10 seconds / 20 / 40 / ip_path (ip also supported); local Rust counters min_form_time / max_page_time / skip_authenticated / honeypot_field 1.0 seconds / 240 seconds / true / empty field; memory timing per engine geo_allow / geo_block / blocklist Empty; blocklist IP maps to Unix expiry seconds, 0 permanent. Unknown country allowed static_keywords / dynamic_keywords / legitimate_keywords / learning Native vocabulary / empty / exact legitimate route names / true; bounded probe learning allowed_methods / uuid_prefix / uuid_window / uuid_threshold No restriction / /user/ / 60 seconds / 5; malformed UUID rejected required_headers / header_min_score HTTP_USER_AGENT and HTTP_ACCEPT / 3; safety caps retained anomaly_window / max_history / max_clients / max_pending 60 seconds / 1000 / 100000 / 10000; bounded local state block_duration 86400 seconds for new blocks; separate from legacy reputation escalation logFsync defaults to false; logging remains immediate. persistBlocks defaults to true and syncs block/keyword event rows immediately, replaying them at startup. This does not provide live cross-worker sharing; use separate files per worker. Legacy Redis/ORM/custom callbacks, manifests and uppercase settings are not imported. Read the native lifecycle , configuration , deployment and measurements , and migration . Shared Python CSV storage List APIs and command help now use blocklist and allowlist . Earlier import/method/command spellings remain compatibility aliases. Existing CSV filenames and Django model identity are retained so upgrades preserve stored blocks and exemptions; use the package storage constants rather than constructing filenames. Python 1.1.4 standardizes Flask, FastAPI, Django CSV mode, and the explicit native pipeline on blacklist.csv , whitelist.csv , keywords.csv , geo_blocked_countries.csv , and path_exemptions.csv . Keyword frequencies and non-policy runtime history are retained in runtime_metadata.csv . Memory, JSON-file, database, and Django ORM modes keep their existing storage behavior. Integration CSV directory configuration Legacy Flask Set app.config['AIWAF_USE_CSV'] = True and app.config['AIWAF_DATA_DIR'] before initializing AIWAF. Legacy Django Set AIWAF_STORAGE_MODE = "csv" and AIWAF_DATA_DIR in project settings. Legacy FastAPI Pass storage={"backend": "csv", "data_dir": "/absolute/path/aiwaf_data"} to AIWAF . Its default backend remains memory. Native adapters Pass the lowercase data_dir in the dedicated native profile. Native adapters do not inherit legacy framework settings. Startup imports legacy runtime CSV data once, preserving block expiry and metadata. Original sources remain intact; backups and completion markers support recovery and prevent removed entries from returning on restart. Existing canonical policy wins conflicts. Stop old workers before upgrading and use the same absolute directory for the application and CLI. See migration paths and recovery . Flask management searches existing project aiwaf_data and .aiwaf/data before user/package directories. Explicit AIWAF_DATA_DIR or --data-dir takes priority. The five policy files use UTF-8 across Python and Rust. Sharing these files does not make memory rate buckets, model history, or optional memory form timing distributed. Flask and FastAPI native honeypot cache Python 1.1.8 with aiwaf-rust 0.2.7 adds opt-in Redis and supplied-cache timing to both native adapters. CSV remains their default. Rust retains timing rules and exemptions; only timestamp I/O uses the cache. import os profile = { "data_dir": "aiwaf_data", "honeypot_backend": "redis", "honeypot_redis_url": os.environ["AIWAF_REDIS_URL"], "honeypot_cache_namespace": "myapp:honeypot:v1", } # Flask: from aiwaf.flask.csv_pipeline import NativeAIWAF NativeAIWAF(app, config=profile) # FastAPI alternative: # from aiwaf.fast.csv_pipeline import NativeAIWAFMiddleware # app.add_middleware(NativeAIWAFMiddleware, config=profile) For Flask-Caching or a compatible custom object, use honeypot_backend="cache" and pass honeypot_cache=cache to the native adapter. It must provide synchronous get(key) and set(key, value, timeout=seconds) , preserve the timestamp/expiry pair, honor TTL and propagate errors. A false write result means failure; silent/no-op backends are unsuitable. Local caches remain worker-local. Use a shared backend and the same namespace across workers; isolate unrelated applications with different namespaces. Records have a 300-second TTL. Missing/evicted timestamps allow the timing check, while cache errors and invalid records return generic HTTP 503. Expired-page POSTs return 409 until a new GET or TTL expiry; old snapshots are not deleted. FastAPI runs cache-backed native checks in its worker thread pool so synchronous cache I/O does not block the event loop. Other policy stores and legacy middleware behavior are unchanged. Django native honeypot cache Python 1.1.8 with aiwaf-rust 0.2.7 defaults Django native honeypot timing to Django's configured cache. Set honeypot_cache_alias in AIWAF_CSV_PIPELINE to select an alias; it defaults to default . Rust calls a small Python cache adapter for timestamp I/O and retains timing decisions, logical expiry and exemptions. Other policy CSVs and rate-limit configuration are unchanged. AIWAF_CSV_PIPELINE = { "data_dir": "aiwaf_data", "honeypot_cache_alias": "default", } # Configure CACHES["default"] with a shared backend for multiple workers. Redis or Memcached can share timestamps across workers. LocMemCache is supported with a startup warning; it remains worker-local. DummyCache is rejected when honeypot protection is enabled. Cache errors, failed writes and invalid records produce generic HTTP 503; known ignored-cache-error modes are rejected. Entries use a 300-second TTL. Expired-page POSTs return 409 until a new GET or TTL expiry. No eager deletion occurs, so an old POST cannot erase a concurrent refresh. A missing or evicted timestamp allows the POST timing check, as before; cache failure is not treated as a miss. Backends do not transfer existing timestamps. Install the matching Rust extension and restart workers together. Explicit honeypot_backend="csv" retains filesystem timing; "memory" uses Rust's per-engine map. Flask, FastAPI and direct native construction keep CSV as the default. See the Django cache documentation . Training replay protection Python 1.1.6 with aiwaf-rust 0.2.5 uses Rust-owned receipts in Flask, FastAPI, and Django. Reusing requests already handled by training cannot extend or recreate a block. Fresh requests must independently satisfy enforcement rules; models and keyword learning can still reuse historical logs. Keep training_evidence.json across expiry, manual unblocking, log rotation, and restarts. It lives in the policy data directory unless AIWAF_TRAINING_STATE_DIR selects another durable directory. Trainers sharing a blocklist must share that directory. Receipts start with this release and cannot reconstruct decisions made by older versions. Missing native support and corrupt state stop training visibly. Block and receipt writes are separate, so a crash between them can require recovery. Flask CLI listing now filters expired entries without rewriting an older snapshot over blocks concurrently added or refreshed by a trainer. The CLI displays the canonical added_date , with the older timestamp as a fallback. This listing fix and training replay protection address different causes of block changes. A first temporary block defaults to 900 seconds; later reputation decisions can increase its duration. Check the stored expiry rather than assuming every block lasts 24 hours.

title: Frequently Asked Questions
text: Frequently Asked Questions How AIWAF works: system architecture Where is the source code? Python, Node.js, Rust/WASM, and Java are in the AIWAF monorepo . The root README is authoritative, and each package has its own version and release tag. Can businesses use AIWAF? Yes. The development checkout and future releases expressly distributed under Elastic License 2.0 permit commercial use, modification, redistribution, and consulting, subject to the license conditions. Providing substantial AIWAF functionality to others as a hosted or managed service requires separate permission. ELv2 also prohibits bypassing license-key functionality and removing required notices. Python and Node.js AIWAF will use ELv2 from version 1.1.2 onward . Other packages have independent version numbers. Previously distributed MIT copies retain their MIT permissions. Check the LICENSE and NOTICE in your installed release: retained MIT contributions, dependencies, and the IPinfo Lite database keep their separate terms. The database is provided by IPinfo under CC BY-SA 4.0 . ELv2-covered code is source available. What do I install for Node.js? Use npm install aiwaf and require('aiwaf') . See the Node.js setup guide . Is PHP included? The current monorepo has no PHP implementation or PHP release workflow. Existing PHP pages are retained as legacy reference and are not current setup guidance. Is Rust required for Python? Python 1.1.8 requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.7 ; installation brings in the Rust runtime. The complete native CSV pipeline still requires an explicit adapter. Legacy integrations do not automatically switch to it. Python retains framework transport, route/authentication facts, GeoIP and management interfaces. See the native architecture . Can I reuse old pickle or joblib models? Current Python model persistence uses JSON. Regenerate executable object artifacts through the current trainer. Java supports Python Rust-model JSON state and restricted legacy signed Java artifacts. JavaScript model implementations remain language-native; do not assume every runtime can exchange models. Does an in-memory backend share protection across workers? In-memory state is process-local. Configure shared storage where consistent multi-worker enforcement is required. Java 1.3.0 supports standalone Redis with atomic enforcement, failure policies, bounded waits, and schema compatibility checks. What are the hardware requirements? AIWAF does not prescribe the previously listed RAM, AVX2, or disk requirements. Use a runtime compatible with the package dependencies and size the deployment for traffic, logging, training, and model workloads. Java targets Java 17; the Python package requires Python 3.10 or newer. The Rust ABI3 extension separately supports Python 3.8 or newer. How does training update protection? Offline training parses configured logs, extracts six features, trains after volume thresholds are met, and refreshes learned keywords while excluding legitimate routes. Schedule training in your deployment; the repo does not promise a real-time external threat-intelligence feed. How do I investigate false positives? Review request logs, trusted-proxy handling, header requirements, rate limits, and path policies. Use narrowly scoped route exemptions and representative staging requests. Check framework CLI status and verify the application object imported for route discovery.

title: Getting started with AIWAF
text: Getting started with AIWAF Build a small protected application, see an enforced request boundary, and then learn how middleware, route policy, state, and training fit together. Start with a complete application The first-app tutorial uses Flask so every file and command can be shown in full. It needs Python and a terminal; it does not assume an existing project, Redis service or trained model. Python 1.1.4 installs its required Rust runtime. Prepare your environment — create a workspace and install the Flask extra. Create your application — understand app.py, registration, and the generated files. Discover live routes — use module:object imports and inspect the manifest. Verify a rate limit — observe three 200 responses and a fourth 429. Add a route policy — exempt one check on one endpoint. Inspect logs and plan training — distinguish observations, counters, and models. Integrate an existing application Each framework guide identifies its prerequisites, the file to edit, the adapter's registration point, the run command, and what to inspect. Use the guide for your framework rather than translating option names between runtimes. Runtime Framework guides Configuration surface Python Flask , Django , FastAPI Flask app.config; Django settings.py; FastAPI nested options Node.js Express , Fastify , Hapi , Koa , NestJS , Next.js API routes , AdonisJS , Sails Adapter options and normalized aliases Java Spring , Jakarta Servlet Typed fields, JSON/environment settings, Spring properties Rust/WASM Primitive bindings Host adapter configuration and primitive API arguments Understand what happens to a request System architecture follows the adapter, policy selection, deterministic controls, runtime state, response observations, and offline training. Continue with Python , Node , Java , or Rust/WASM internals for implementation boundaries. Look up a specific task Configuration reference : settings, types, source defaults, precedence, and shared state. Upgrade guide : package rename, reputation state, manifests, and models. Troubleshooting : rejected imports, missing routes, unexpected blocks, and training inputs. API entry points : runtime APIs and the distinction from website administration. Choose packages deliberately Python and npm both use the name aiwaf . The required Rust runtime for Python 1.1.4 is aiwaf-rust ; WebAssembly primitives are aiwaf-wasm . title: Java Architecture and Response-Aware Enforcement
text: Java Architecture and Response-Aware Enforcement The native Java engine consumes an AiwafRequest and returns an AiwafDecision. Spring and Servlet integrations map HTTP traffic into that contract; storage contexts and model providers are owned by the engine. On this page The engine contracts Two-stage Spring execution Inside the pre-response engine Discovery and configuration before requests arrive Per-engine state and atomic Redis operations Redis failure and upgrade boundaries Response-derived UUID and anomaly evidence Worked example: a missing UUID resource Trace the implementation How AIWAF works: system architecture The engine contracts Contract Purpose AiwafRequest Normalized method, path, client, country, headers, parameters, timing context, and disabled middleware metadata. AiwafConfig Typed limits, exemptions, path rules, storage, model, and observability settings. AiwafDecision Allow or deny outcome with a response status and reason. AiwafEngine Orchestrates checks using its storage context, model provider, UUID lookup, and telemetry. The engine is independent of a controller or servlet response object. Adapters decide how to map an engine decision into HTTP behavior. Java runs natively and does not load the Rust extension. Two-stage Spring execution Map and inspect Discover route metadata, buffer permitted request data, and construct AiwafRequest. Before response evaluateBeforeResponse runs deterministic controls and can prevent controller execution. Controller The allowed request traverses the normal filter chain. After response Use actual status and duration for UUID behavior and anomaly evaluation when the response is still replaceable. AiwafFilter sends an early error for a pre-response denial. After a synchronous handler, it checks whether the response is committed. An uncommitted response can be reset and replaced if the final decision denies it. A committed response is recorded through recordCommittedResponse . Asynchronous completion uses a listener and records once. These paths update relevant history and logs without trying to replace output that has already been sent. The request-only evaluate(request) API remains available and uses provisional status and timing for its AI features. The generic Servlet filter uses that request-time path; Spring's filter has the richer response-aware boundary. Inside the pre-response engine Validate request shape, compressed-body policy, and prohibited Java-serialization payloads. Resolve the path rule, rate overrides, and path/IP exemption state. Reject active blocklisted clients unless the client exemption applies. Enforce the configured method policy. Run applicable keyword, UUID, honeypot, header, geo, and rate/flood checks. Return an allow decision, deferring anomaly scoring for the two-stage API. Each failing stage finalizes a decision and returns early. Path exemptions do not bypass the initial request-shape and method gates, and an exempt path does not automatically bypass an active client blocklist. Geo-only exemptions disable geo enforcement without implying a complete bypass. Discovery and configuration before requests arrive Spring Boot servlet auto-configuration creates the configuration, engine, and ordered filter unless the application supplies replacements. The live MVC mappings expose registered routes and handler annotations. This lets the filter honor route metadata without maintaining a separate controller list. Manifest generation writes discovered routes and policy metadata; PathManifestCore loads and compiles it for the engine. Generated rules are appended after explicit path rules, preserving explicit equal-prefix precedence. Optional JPA metamodel discovery supplies UUID-valued primary-key and unique-property lookup. JSON configuration uses the shared nested setting vocabulary. Environment variables and Spring properties overlay file values. Configuration loading decides the engine's policy and dependencies before request evaluation begins. Per-engine state and atomic Redis operations Each engine holds a RuntimeStorage.Context . The context combines typed operational stores with RuntimeState for rate counters, form timing, UUID scores, and recent behavior. Creating another engine does not replace the first engine's context. Backend Ownership Behavior across application instances Memory Local engine state. No shared enforcement across instances. File, CSV, SQLite Local persistent store with per-engine request state. Persistence alone does not distribute every request counter. Standalone Redis Shared namespace with versioned keys. Atomic server-side operations coordinate rate, form, UUID, and anomaly state as well as operational stores. The static storage and blocklist helpers remain compatibility facades for CLI and administrative usage; the engine evaluates requests against its own context. Redis failure and upgrade boundaries Java 1.3 supports standalone Redis and validates unsupported Sentinel or Cluster configurations rather than pretending they provide equivalent semantics. Connection, socket, pool-size, and pool-wait limits bound the request's wait for state. fail_closed prevents startup or raises a request-path storage failure when Redis is unavailable. fail_open uses nonblocking enforcement fallbacks and reports failed mutations at the storage boundary. These policies change availability behavior, not model semantics. Versioned keys and a namespace compatibility marker prevent incompatible state schemas from sharing one prefix during an upgrade. A schema mismatch refuses the namespace even under fail_open . Use separate prefixes for separate applications, environments, or intentionally incompatible schemas. Response-derived UUID and anomaly evidence Malformed UUID input contributes an immediate weighted signal. A valid UUID request that returns 404 adds a different probing signal; successful requests can decay the score. The post-response stage supplies the real outcome instead of treating every request as an assumed success. The lazy model provider loads the configured model on demand or through preloading. Scoring builds the Python-aligned six-feature vector, evaluates the forest, and applies threshold and behavior-confirmation rules. Forest availability and sufficient behavior evidence determine whether the AI path can deny a request. Feature What it describes Why it helps path_len Length of the request path. Unusually long probing paths. kw_hits Matches against malicious keywords. Known probing patterns within a path. resp_time Response duration in seconds. Behavior that differs from the normal timing distribution. status_idx An encoded response-status category. Response outcomes without treating status codes as continuous measurements. burst_count Requests associated with the client in the burst window. Rapid repeated activity. total_404 Not-found responses in the relevant per-client history. Repeated discovery of nonexistent routes. The feature order is part of the model contract. A trainer and scorer must agree on the order, status mapping, time units, and window semantics. Summary fields ending in _ms use milliseconds; the feature vector uses seconds. Sharing feature names alone does not make every model artifact interchangeable. New Java models persist safe JSON containing the supported Python Rust-model forest state. Restricted signed legacy Java models remain compatibility inputs, including older feature schemas. A schema match must be checked before exchanging an artifact. Worked example: a missing UUID resource A valid UUID request passes deterministic checks and reaches a Spring controller. The controller returns 404. If the response is uncommitted, the filter supplies that status and duration to the post-response engine. The engine updates weighted UUID behavior, evaluates eligible anomaly evidence, records recent history, and returns the final decision. If the controller already streamed its response, the committed path records the result without replacing it. The observed 404 still matters for subsequent behavior. System overview explains the broader feedback loop; operations covers Redis and model administration. Trace the implementation Follow these files in the monorepo to connect the architecture to the code: java/src/main/java/com/aiwaf/core/AiwafEngine.java java/src/main/java/com/aiwaf/spring/AiwafFilter.java java/src/main/java/com/aiwaf/core/PathManifestCore.java java/src/main/java/com/aiwaf/runtime/RuntimeStorage.java java/src/main/java/com/aiwaf/runtime/RedisStorage.java

title: Java Storage and Operations
text: Java Storage and Operations How AIWAF works: system architecture Version and source build Java 1.3.0 adds hardened Redis operation to the scoped distributed state introduced in 1.2.0 . The version in java/pom.xml describes the source checkout; verify Maven Central availability before adding that version to an application. git clone https://github.com/aiwaf-project/aiwaf.git cd aiwaf/java mvn test mvn -Dgpg.skip=true package Configuration, Redis, and operational commands Area Main AiwafConfig fields Rate limiting rateLimitEnabled , rateLimitScope , rateLimitWindowSeconds , rateLimitMax , rateLimitFloodThreshold Headers headerValidationEnabled , requiredHeadersByMethod , minHeaderQualityScore , size/count limits Request body, parameter, method, and content-type limits Proxies trustedProxyCidrs , maxForwardedForEntries Exemptions exemptIps , exemptPaths , autoExemptPathPrefixes GeoIP geoBlockEnabled , geoAllowedCountries , geoBlockedCountries , geoIpDatabasePath , cache limits Route manifest pathManifestEnabled , pathManifestPath , pathRules UUID checks uuidTamperEnabled , uuidScoreWindowSeconds , uuidScoreBlockThreshold , signal weights, uuidParameterNames AI aiEnabled , aiModelPath , aiAnomalyScoreThreshold Storage storageBackend , storageFilePath , storageRedisUrl , storageKeyPrefix , storageRedisFailureMode , Redis timeout and pool limits Telemetry observabilityEnabled GeoIP uses the bundled MMDB through the native Java reader; it does not require the external mmdblookup executable. A valid X-Country value is accepted only from a peer in trustedProxyCidrs ; otherwise AIWAF resolves the client address itself. Default blocklist calls use Python-compatible reputation scoring and temporary escalation (15 minutes, 1 hour, then 24 hours). Use BlocklistManager.blockPermanent(ip, reason) for an explicit permanent administrative block. storageBackend="redis" makes rate-limit buckets, honeypot timing, weighted UUID scores, recent-request anomaly state, blocklist data, exemptions, geo policy, and learned keywords visible to every application instance using the same key prefix. Redis enforcement updates use atomic server-side scripts. Memory, file, CSV, and SQLite engines keep request state isolated per AiwafEngine ; constructing another engine no longer replaces an existing engine's stores. The static RuntimeStorage and BlocklistManager methods remain compatibility facades for command-line and administrative code. The Java 1.3 Redis backend supports standalone Redis only . Sentinel and Cluster configurations are rejected during validation instead of silently operating with incomplete semantics. fail_closed is the default: an unavailable Redis instance prevents startup or raises a request-path storage failure, which results in the application denying availability rather than bypassing protection. fail_open permits startup and returns non-blocking enforcement fallbacks while Redis is unavailable; failed mutations return false at the StorageBackend boundary. Connection, socket, pool size, and pool wait limits are bounded and configurable. RedisStorage.diagnostics() reports operation/failure counts, latency, and live pool utilization. Redis keys include a state-schema version, and each base key prefix has an atomic compatibility marker. Releases using the same schema can share state during a rolling upgrade. A runtime with an incompatible schema refuses the namespace—even in fail_open mode. Use a unique key prefix per application and environment; deploy an incompatible schema with a new prefix, migrate deliberately, then retire the old namespace. Serialized persistent values remain JSON within a schema version. New Java models use the Python-aligned six-feature schema and are written as safe JSON containing the Python aiwaf_rust.IsolationForest state. Python can restore Java-generated forest state, and Java can load Python Rust-model artifacts. Existing signed Java binary artifacts, including nine-feature models, remain readable through the restricted legacy loader. Scikit-learn object artifacts are intentionally unsupported. Java operational commands mirror the common Python workflow: aiwaf-cli status aiwaf-cli diagnose --model model.json aiwaf-cli blocked aiwaf-cli unblock 203.0.113.10 aiwaf-cli clear aiwaf-cli train --events events.json --out model.json --backend java aiwaf-cli replay --cases replay.json aiwaf-cli model status --path model.json aiwaf-cli logs --dir aiwaf_logs Build Java from the repository root: cd java mvn test mvn -Dgpg.skip=true package The build produces the main, source, and Javadoc JARs under java/target/ . The main JAR embeds the root license as META-INF/LICENSE . FastR training is optional and falls back to the Java trainer when R or jsonlite is unavailable. Spring property examples Spring Boot applications are protected automatically. Adding aiwaf-java creates AiwafConfig , AiwafEngine , and the ordered AiwafFilter ; discovers live MVC routes, route annotations, and JPA UUID fields; and applies request controls before the controller plus post-response scoring with the real status and timing. Set aiwaf.enabled=false to disable auto-configuration. aiwaf.rate-limit.max=60 aiwaf.rate-limit.window-seconds=60 aiwaf.geo.enabled=true aiwaf.geo.blocked-countries=CN,RU aiwaf.path-manifest.path=.aiwaf/paths.json # Use one namespace and shared enforcement state across application instances. aiwaf.storage.backend=redis aiwaf.storage.redis-url=redis://localhost:6379/0 aiwaf.storage.key-prefix=my-service # Redis is fail-closed by default. Every wait is bounded. aiwaf.storage.redis-failure-mode=fail_closed aiwaf.storage.redis-connection-timeout-millis=1000 aiwaf.storage.redis-socket-timeout-millis=2000 aiwaf.storage.redis-pool-max-total=32 aiwaf.storage.redis-pool-max-idle=16 aiwaf.storage.redis-pool-min-idle=0 aiwaf.storage.redis-pool-max-wait-millis=250 Set aiwaf.config-file=/etc/aiwaf/config.json (or AIWAF_CONFIG_FILE ) to load the same nested JSON configuration used by the Python runtime. Environment variables and Spring properties override file values. AiwafConfigFileCore also exposes load, save, deep-merge, and validation APIs for non-Spring applications. Define an AiwafConfig , AiwafEngine , or AiwafFilter bean only when the application needs a custom replacement. For plain Spring MVC without Boot, register the filter directly; passing the application context enables the same live route discovery: @Bean AiwafFilter aiwafFilter(AiwafEngine engine, ApplicationContext context) { return new AiwafFilter(engine, context); } The live mapping integration honors @AiwafExempt , @AiwafExemptFrom , @AiwafOnly , and @AiwafRequireProtection without a controller list. Do not register AiwafInterceptor and AiwafFilter as independent enforcement layers for the same request. Committed, streaming, and asynchronous responses are recorded but are not replaced after bytes have been sent. UUID protection uses Python-compatible weighted signals: malformed input, valid UUID requests that resolve to 404 , and successful requests that decay the score. UUID-valued query parameters and {uuid} route variables are supported. SpringUuidModelLookup optionally discovers UUID primary keys and unique UUID properties through the JPA metamodel; omit it when the application does not use JPA. Generate a route manifest from the live Spring application rather than supplying controller methods manually: java -cp "your-app.jar:aiwaf-java-1.3.5.jar" \ com.aiwaf.cli.AiwafConsole init \ --app com.example.Application \ --output .aiwaf/paths.json The command starts the application, reads every registered RequestMappingHandlerMapping , writes the shared schema_version/framework/context_hash/routes document, and then closes the temporary application context. Set pathManifestEnabled=false or aiwaf.path-manifest.enabled=false to opt out. Deployment Configure the application to trust forwarding headers only from known proxy CIDRs. Configure the outermost proxy to overwrite client-supplied forwarding headers. Use Redis, a database, or another shared backend when multiple workers must share rate-limit, blocklist, or exemption state. Keep health checks, static assets, and trusted webhook routes explicitly scoped instead of disabling protection globally. Start anomaly detection in observe-only or conservative mode and tune it with representative normal traffic. Rotate logs and exclude secrets, authorization headers, cookies, and personal data. Sign model/configuration artifacts where the runtime supports HMAC verification. Run AIWAF alongside normal secure-development controls and an edge/reverse-proxy layer. Bounded SQL inspection Java SQL inspection defaults to security.sql_injection_mode: "block" ; monitor records findings without denying requests and off disables it. AIWAF_SQL_INJECTION_MODE is the environment override. Inspection honors the configured body-byte limit and returns HTTP 413 when inspection exceeds its budget. Previously learned benign keywords no longer block ordinary routes. Java remains a native Java implementation. October 2026 release upgrade The prepared source versions are Python 1.1.6 , Rust/Python 0.2.5 , Node.js 1.1.4 , WASM 0.2.4 , and Java 1.3.4 . These are source targets; verify registry availability before installing. Python requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.5 , including the TrainingEvidence API. Node offline training requires the matching WASM receipt API. Back up policies, logs, models, and training evidence. Use the same absolute data and evidence directories for application workers and CLI trainers. Install the matching native companion before upgrading its host package: Rust before Python, WASM before Node. Preserve training_evidence.json and node_training_evidence.json across expiry, unblocking, restarts, and log rotation. Stop older file writers and restart all workers on the new code. Mixing old unlocked writers with new writers can still lose updates. In staging, train twice on identical logs, then verify handled evidence does not recreate a removed or expired block. Add genuinely fresh requests and confirm they must independently satisfy the enforcement threshold. Verify that listing and expiry checks preserve concurrently refreshed blocks and unrelated IPs. Check the raw expiry and backend location if entries disappear unexpectedly. Java CSV and file storage Java 1.3.4 reloads current storage under a shared JVM and OS sidecar lock for each operation. Reads filter expiry without rewriting disk; mutations preserve other instances' updates and report persistence failures. This adds file I/O. Java model training still does not add blocklist entries. Rate buckets and other per-engine memory state retain their existing isolation. Lock recovery Python training uses an OS file lock; Java CSV/file OS locks also release on process exit. Keep their stable sidecar lock files in place while workers run. Node uses lock directories for training and legacy CSV mutations; a crash can leave them behind. Confirm the owning process has stopped before removing a Node lock directory. Do not delete training receipts to clear a lock: doing so loses handled-evidence history. Release checks Local validation passed 247 Node tests across 67 suites with the coverage gate, 215 Java tests with 3 skips, and 38 Rust/WASM native tests. After the native dependency bump, 11 affected Python packaging tests passed through the appropriate Django and pytest runners. These checks do not replace full release CI, dependency audits, signing, or operating-system wheel builds. Build Linux/macOS Rust wheels using the release matrix; the local bundle contains a Windows x86-64 wheel. For release maintainers: publish the WASM companion, refresh the Node lockfile from the registry to record its actual integrity, then run npm ci and the native integration checks. Do not substitute an older native dependency to satisfy a stale packaging test. See the changelog .

title: Jakarta Servlet Setup
text: Jakarta Servlet Setup How AIWAF works: system architecture Integrate native Java enforcement into Jakarta Servlet and verify how the adapter observes requests and responses. Before you begin You need Java 17+, Maven, and an existing Jakarta Servlet 6.1 application and a compatible container. These are integration snippets, not a standalone generated application. First confirm that an ordinary endpoint runs without AIWAF. 1. Add the Java dependency pom.xml / dependencies Java source version 1.3.5 is declared in java/pom.xml . It targets Java 17, Spring Framework 7.0, and Jakarta Servlet 6.1, and runs natively without Rust. Use the Maven dependency below once this version is published to Maven Central; source builds are available from the monorepo. <dependency> <groupId>io.github.aiwaf-project</groupId> <artifactId>aiwaf-java</artifactId> <version>1.3.5</version> </dependency> Build from source when needed If the required version is unavailable in your registry, install the reviewed monorepo source in your local Maven repository: git clone https://github.com/aiwaf-project/aiwaf.git cd aiwaf/java mvn -Dgpg.skip=true install Return to your application checkout afterward. Match its dependency version to the version built from java/pom.xml. 2. Understand the engine boundary The following code belongs inside application initialization/request handling, not at the top level of a Java source file. It illustrates the core API; the filter shown next performs this adapter work for Servlet requests. Use the two-stage API when the integration can observe the handler response. Deterministic controls run before the application; anomaly scoring then receives the actual status and elapsed time. import com.aiwaf.core.AiwafConfig; import com.aiwaf.core.AiwafDecision; import com.aiwaf.core.AiwafEngine; import com.aiwaf.core.AiwafRequest; import java.util.Map; import java.util.Set; AiwafConfig config = new AiwafConfig(); config.rateLimitEnabled = true; config.rateLimitMax = 20; config.rateLimitWindowSeconds = 10; AiwafEngine engine = new AiwafEngine(config); AiwafRequest request = new AiwafRequest( "GET", "/api/profile", "203.0.113.10", "US", Map.of("User-Agent", "Mozilla/5.0", "Accept", "application/json"), Map.of(), System.currentTimeMillis(), Set.of() ); long started = System.currentTimeMillis(); AiwafDecision decision = engine.evaluateBeforeResponse(request); if (decision.allowed()) { decision = engine.evaluateAfterResponse( request, 200, System.currentTimeMillis() - started ); } evaluate(request) remains available for request-only integrations and uses provisional response values for AI features. 3. Register the Servlet filter During servlet-context initialization, add the filter before the handlers it protects. Import com.aiwaf.servlet.AiwafServletFilter in the class that owns this initialization. Keep the container's existing initialization and filter ordering. AiwafConfig config = new AiwafConfig(); AiwafEngine engine = new AiwafEngine(config); servletContext .addFilter("aiwaf", new AiwafServletFilter(engine)) .addMappingForUrlPatterns(null, false, "/*"); The generic servlet filter uses request-time evaluation. Spring applications should prefer AiwafFilter for handler metadata and post-response scoring. Configuration and operations Area Main AiwafConfig fields Rate limiting rateLimitEnabled , rateLimitScope , rateLimitWindowSeconds , rateLimitMax , rateLimitFloodThreshold Headers headerValidationEnabled , requiredHeadersByMethod , minHeaderQualityScore , size/count limits Request body, parameter, method, and content-type limits Proxies trustedProxyCidrs , maxForwardedForEntries Exemptions exemptIps , exemptPaths , autoExemptPathPrefixes GeoIP geoBlockEnabled , geoAllowedCountries , geoBlockedCountries , geoIpDatabasePath , cache limits Route manifest pathManifestEnabled , pathManifestPath , pathRules UUID checks uuidTamperEnabled , uuidScoreWindowSeconds , uuidScoreBlockThreshold , signal weights, uuidParameterNames AI aiEnabled , aiModelPath , aiAnomalyScoreThreshold Storage storageBackend , storageFilePath , storageRedisUrl , storageKeyPrefix , storageRedisFailureMode , Redis timeout and pool limits Telemetry observabilityEnabled GeoIP uses the bundled MMDB through the native Java reader; it does not require the external mmdblookup executable. A valid X-Country value is accepted only from a peer in trustedProxyCidrs ; otherwise AIWAF resolves the client address itself. Default blocklist calls use Python-compatible reputation scoring and temporary escalation (15 minutes, 1 hour, then 24 hours). Use BlocklistManager.blockPermanent(ip, reason) for an explicit permanent administrative block. storageBackend="redis" makes rate-limit buckets, honeypot timing, weighted UUID scores, recent-request anomaly state, blocklist data, exemptions, geo policy, and learned keywords visible to every application instance using the same key prefix. Redis enforcement updates use atomic server-side scripts. Memory, file, CSV, and SQLite engines keep request state isolated per AiwafEngine ; constructing another engine no longer replaces an existing engine's stores. The static RuntimeStorage and BlocklistManager methods remain compatibility facades for command-line and administrative code. The Java 1.3 Redis backend supports standalone Redis only . Sentinel and Cluster configurations are rejected during validation instead of silently operating with incomplete semantics. fail_closed is the default: an unavailable Redis instance prevents startup or raises a request-path storage failure, which results in the application denying availability rather than bypassing protection. fail_open permits startup and returns non-blocking enforcement fallbacks while Redis is unavailable; failed mutations return false at the StorageBackend boundary. Connection, socket, pool size, and pool wait limits are bounded and configurable. RedisStorage.diagnostics() reports operation/failure counts, latency, and live pool utilization. Redis keys include a state-schema version, and each base key prefix has an atomic compatibility marker. Releases using the same schema can share state during a rolling upgrade. A runtime with an incompatible schema refuses the namespace—even in fail_open mode. Use a unique key prefix per application and environment; deploy an incompatible schema with a new prefix, migrate deliberately, then retire the old namespace. Serialized persistent values remain JSON within a schema version. New Java models use the Python-aligned six-feature schema and are written as safe JSON containing the Python aiwaf_rust.IsolationForest state. Python can restore Java-generated forest state, and Java can load Python Rust-model artifacts. Existing signed Java binary artifacts, including nine-feature models, remain readable through the restricted legacy loader. Scikit-learn object artifacts are intentionally unsupported. Java operational commands mirror the common Python workflow: aiwaf-cli status aiwaf-cli diagnose --model model.json aiwaf-cli blocked aiwaf-cli unblock 203.0.113.10 aiwaf-cli clear aiwaf-cli train --events events.json --out model.json --backend java aiwaf-cli replay --cases replay.json aiwaf-cli model status --path model.json aiwaf-cli logs --dir aiwaf_logs Build Java from the repository root: cd java mvn test mvn -Dgpg.skip=true package The build produces the main, source, and Javadoc JARs under java/target/ . The main JAR embeds the root license as META-INF/LICENSE . FastR training is optional and falls back to the Java trainer when R or jsonlite is unavailable. Start the application with its existing launcher and request a known non-exempt handler through a browser. Inspect the enabled policy, observed client IP, response status, and duration. Private-address exemptions can affect local tests. Exercise a deliberate block or rate boundary on a staging route, and confirm the handler response is not returned for the rejected request. title: AIWAF for Node.js
text: AIWAF for Node.js Current Node source and framework support The source candidate is aiwaf 1.1.5 with the declared aiwaf-wasm ^0.2.5 dependency. Publish the matching WASM companion first. The native request engine still requires explicit registration and awaits initialization; a missing native API fails startup. Legacy adapters keep their separate configuration and execution path. Offline training now uses WASM receipts to prevent handled historical requests from extending or recreating blocks after expiry or manual removal. Models still fit on history; enforcement uses fresh requests. Preserve node_training_evidence.json in the blocklist data directory, or set AIWAF_TRAINING_STATE_DIR to a durable shared directory. Invalid timestamps are excluded. Missing WASM APIs, corrupt receipts, and storage failures make training fail visibly. A crashed trainer can leave node_training_evidence.lock ; confirm it has stopped before removing that lock directory. Block and receipt writes are separate, so a crash between them can require recovery. The current reference tests use Node 22.18.0 , Express 4, Fastify 5, and NestJS 11. These are tested configurations, not a claim that every framework version is supported. Use the framework and adapter matching your application. Next.js examples require Node API request/response objects; Edge middleware is not supported by this adapter. Legacy blocklist request checks and listing are read-only. Explicit database cleanup checks expiry in the DELETE statement; CSV cleanup reads current rows under the same cross-process lock used by blocklist writes. A crash can leave <blocklist CSV path>.lock ; confirm its writer has stopped before removing that directory. Lock acquisition fails after 60 seconds. Restart all old writers when upgrading. These fixes do not make the explicit native engine's per-worker state distributed. For source development, use the committed lockfile with npm ci , run the coverage and real native checks, and audit the complete tree with npm audit . Read dependency versions and verification and native migration . Native request pipeline Native mode: Node source candidate aiwaf 1.1.5 declares aiwaf-wasm ^0.2.5 . Explicit native registration validates NativeRequestPipeline at startup; missing or incompatible support is an error. There is no JavaScript policy fallback for this engine. Installing the dependency does not switch an existing legacy middleware chain. The explicit native adapter validates configuration once, then Rust/WASM owns geo/blocklist/keyword/structured SQL decisions, rate and flood counters, honeypot timing, UUID scores, anomaly history/model inference, keyword learning and CSV formatting. Node retains framework facts, bounded body parsing, response handling and filesystem writes with cached file descriptors. Existing integrations keep their legacy middleware path. Read the native lifecycle , configuration , deployment and measurements , and migration . How AIWAF works: system architecture The CommonJS npm package is aiwaf , source candidate 1.1.2 in js/package.json . Install with npm install aiwaf and import with require('aiwaf') . All adapters share the monorepo and root README. Express quick start const express = require('express'); const aiwaf = require('aiwaf'); const app = express(); app.use(express.json()); app.use(aiwaf({ AIWAF_MIDDLEWARES: ['auto'], staticKeywords: ['.php', '.env', '.git'], WINDOW_SEC: 10, MAX_REQ: 20, FLOOD_REQ: 40, AIWAF_HEADER_VALIDATION: true, AIWAF_METHOD_POLICY_ENABLED: true, AIWAF_ALLOWED_METHODS: ['GET', 'POST', 'HEAD', 'OPTIONS'] })); app.get('/', (req, res) => res.json({ protected: true })); app.listen(3000); Attach AIWAF after the body parser when honeypot rules inspect parsed form or JSON fields. Framework entry points Framework Entry point Express aiwaf(options) Fastify fastify.register(aiwaf.fastify, options) Hapi server.register({ plugin: aiwaf.hapi, options }) Koa app.use(aiwaf.koa(options)) NestJS/Express aiwaf.nest(options) or the Express middleware NestJS/Fastify app.register(aiwaf.fastify, options) Next.js API routes aiwaf.next(handler, options) AdonisJS aiwaf.adonis(options) Sails.js aiwaf.sails(options) Route policies app.use(aiwaf({ AIWAF_PATH_RULES: [ { PREFIX: '/health/', DISABLE: ['header_validation', 'rate_limit'] }, { PREFIX: '/api/public/', RATE_LIMIT: { WINDOW: 60, MAX: 300 } } ] })); Applications can also use aiwaf.exempt , aiwaf.exemptFrom , aiwaf.only , and aiwaf.requireProtection to build route policies. Generate an Express route manifest after routes are registered: aiwaf.generateExpressManifest(app, '.aiwaf/paths.json'); Or generate one from a route list with the CLI: cd js npm run aiwaf -- manifest --framework express --routes routes.json --output .aiwaf/paths.json Configuration and acceleration Area Important options Middleware AIWAF_MIDDLEWARES , AIWAF_DISABLE_MIDDLEWARES , AIWAF_PATH_RULES Rate limiting WINDOW_SEC , MAX_REQ , FLOOD_REQ , cache Headers AIWAF_HEADER_VALIDATION , AIWAF_REQUIRED_HEADERS , AIWAF_HEADER_QUALITY_MIN_SCORE Methods AIWAF_METHOD_POLICY_ENABLED , AIWAF_ALLOWED_METHODS Keywords staticKeywords , AIWAF_ENABLE_KEYWORD_LEARNING , AIWAF_DYNAMIC_TOP_N Honeypot HONEYPOT_FIELD , timing settings GeoIP AIWAF_GEO_BLOCK_ENABLED , AIWAF_GEO_BLOCK_COUNTRIES , AIWAF_GEO_ALLOW_COUNTRIES Models AIWAF_MODEL_STORAGE , AIWAF_MODEL_PATH , AIWAF_MODEL_CACHE_KEY Logging AIWAF_MIDDLEWARE_LOGGING , AIWAF_MIDDLEWARE_LOG_PATH , DB/CSV options WASM AIWAF_WASM_VALIDATION , AIWAF_WASM_VALIDATE_RECENT AIWAF loads aiwaf-wasm when available and falls back to the JavaScript implementation when WASM initialization or conversion is not worthwhile. Small, object-heavy operations can be faster in JavaScript because crossing the JS/WASM boundary and serializing objects has a fixed cost. WASM is most useful for sufficiently large feature batches and model scoring workloads. Continue Framework setup Architecture Operations

These fixes do not make the explicit native engine's per-worker state distributed.
