Read dependency versions and verification and native migration . Rust-owned Node request engine Native mode: Node source candidate aiwaf 1.1.5 declares aiwaf-wasm ^0.2.5 . Explicit native registration validates NativeRequestPipeline at startup; missing or incompatible support is an error. There is no JavaScript policy fallback for this engine. Installing the dependency does not switch an existing legacy middleware chain. The explicit native adapter validates configuration once, then Rust/WASM owns geo/blocklist/keyword/structured SQL decisions, rate and flood counters, honeypot timing, UUID scores, anomaly history/model inference, keyword learning and CSV formatting. Node retains framework facts, bounded body parsing, response handling and filesystem writes with cached file descriptors. Existing integrations keep their legacy middleware path. Startup Validate the native API and immutable profile, replay dedicated persisted state, optionally snapshot a trained model, and open CSV writers. Begin in WASM Node passes one normalized request envelope; Rust applies enabled protections and returns an engine-owned context with its decision. Application Node dispatches allowed requests or constructs a denial. Parsed bodies are bounded before inspection. Finish in WASM At response finish/close, Rust updates response-dependent state and emits escaped CSV rows; Node appends them immediately. Execution order and transport geo_block → ip_keyword_block → rate_limit → ai_anomaly → honeypot → uuid_tamper → header_validation → logging . SQL traversal is bounded by bytes, nodes and depth; nested serialized JSON and double URL escapes are inspected. Unknown routes still receive applicable checks. Profile-level exemptions are global; required route metadata overrides route decorator exemptions. Express/Sails use await aiwaf.native(options) . Other Node adapters accept the sole outer option AIWAF_NATIVE_PIPELINE: options . Fastify runs after parsing at preValidation, including its not-found handler. Hapi begins at onRequest so unknown routes are covered, then makes an additional native body/authentication timing check at onPreHandler. Koa, Nest, Adonis and Next use their existing transport wrappers. This is Node API-handler integration, not an Edge/Fetch middleware. State and persistence Rate buckets, form timestamps, UUID scores, anomaly history and policy snapshots are per engine/worker. Blocks and learned keywords append to dedicated synced CSV files and reload at startup. They are not live synchronized across workers and do not use the legacy ORM/reputation/CLI schemas. Use separate data/log paths per worker; use the legacy integration when live shared Redis/custom stores are required. Immediate logging has no in-memory batch queue. Log fsync is optional; policy event writes sync immediately. Rust formats CSV; WASM does not directly open or mutate host files. Elapsed time is monotonic; aborted responses log 499, engine contexts finalize once, and unused payloads are not retained during streaming responses. Model contract Pass a fitted six-feature Rust/WASM forest as model. The engine snapshots it; setModel(model) replaces the snapshot and setModel(null) disables inference. Node retains [pathLen, kwHits, statusIdx, responseTime, burst, total404] with milliseconds, distinct from Python. Response-time inference/behavior gates can block subsequent requests; they cannot retract a completed response. Without a model, history and learning remain active. Source map rust/crates/aiwaf_wasm/src/request_pipeline.rs : immutable profile, state, inspection and CSV formatting. rust/crates/aiwaf_wasm/src/lib.rs : NativeRequestPipeline bindings. js/lib/nativePipeline.js : transport facts, startup and immediate host writes. js/lib/wasmAdapter.js : one-time API/model binding. Read the native lifecycle , configuration , deployment and measurements , and migration . On this page Adapter boundary Middleware construction and request planning Actual enforcement sequence What unknown-route anomaly detection means Route analysis becomes a per-request plan State and process boundaries Response hooks and offline learning Optional WASM execution Worked example: one denied request Trace the implementation How AIWAF works: system architecture Adapter boundary js/index.js exports the main middleware and Fastify, Hapi, Koa, NestJS, Next.js API-route, AdonisJS, and Sails adapters. Each adapter maps its framework's request and response methods into the core contract and translates an early rejection back into the framework. Body parsing must happen before protections that inspect parsed fields. Next.js integration uses the Node-style API-handler contract; a Fetch API or Edge request is a different boundary. An adapter is responsible for continuation and response completion, not for maintaining a separate policy implementation. Middleware construction and request planning wafMiddleware.js normalizes configuration, loads path rules, initializes check modules, and creates the middleware function. Each request resolves its path, method, client address, and route plan. shouldApply combines global middleware selection with the route plan. The logger is attached before the ordinary checks when enabled. A shared denial helper records the reason and sends a status with a JSON or text error according to the request and configuration. A rejected request returns early instead of calling the downstream handler. Legacy enforcement sequence The current core executes the following sequence for a request. Individual layers run only when enabled and applicable: Attach logging and request timing; resolve the route plan. Enforce the global method policy when enabled. This happens before the request-exemption shortcut. Check IP/path exemptions, then the active blocklist. Validate headers and any enabled WASM header, URL, content, or recent-behavior checks. Apply geo policy, honeypot timing, and rate/flood limits. Inspect static and learned malicious keywords, then UUID probing. Evaluate the eligible unknown-route anomaly path. Attach completed-response keyword learning and call next() for an allowed request. Method rejection can return 405 ; ordinary rate excess can return 429 ; blocklist and other blocking paths can return 403 . The configured checks decide whether a denial also changes IP reputation. What unknown-route anomaly detection means The core compares the requested path with discoverable Express-style routes. If the route table is unavailable or empty, it treats the request as known rather than applying aggressive unknown-route anomaly detection to every proxied request. For an eligible unknown route, the anomaly module scores features. A positive model result alone is insufficient: the model must meet training-volume requirements and recent-behavior analysis must confirm scanning-related activity before the core issues its anomaly block. This gate explains why a suspicious score and an actual denial can differ. Route analysis becomes a per-request plan sourceAst.js uses bounded handler-source analysis to infer API, form, and authentication intent. pathManifest.js combines source signals with live framework route extraction. The compiler turns discovered protections into path overrides; it does not take over the framework router. pathRules.js evaluates those rules with route metadata for each request. Explicit policy can disable one check or override rate limits for a prefix. Rebuilding a manifest is a discovery operation; enforcing its compiled policy is a runtime operation. State and process boundaries Module group State or computation Scope to consider rateLimiter.js Recent timestamps for request-rate windows. An external cache can share the window; the fallback cache is local. Block, exemption, keyword, and geo stores Operational policy and learned data. SQLite and CSV persistence paths differ from distributed request state. anomalyDetector.js and modelStore.js Loaded model and recent behavior. A shared model artifact does not automatically share every behavior buffer. middlewareLogger.js Completed requests and denial reasons. Log persistence supplies evidence and input for offline training. The rate-limiter module initializes its cache from configuration and otherwise uses a process-local fallback. Configure shared state deliberately when multiple Node workers must enforce one limit. Response hooks and offline learning For allowed requests, a response finish hook supplies the actual status to keyword learning. That hook runs after the handler response finishes; it cannot undo an already delivered response. The middleware logger also observes completion. Request logs Completed responses supply paths, client identity, status, and timing. Feature extraction Records are normalized and combined with per-client activity windows. Train and review Volume thresholds gate model training; route exemptions filter learned keywords. Publish artifacts The runtime loads persisted model state and updated learned keywords. The training job is separate from ordinary application request handling. Reading logs and rebuilding a forest does not need to happen for every request. Runtime keyword learning, where enabled, is a separate mechanism that can use completed-response signals. Offline training reads configured access logs or middleware records and persists a language-native forest artifact. Review feature and model compatibility before moving artifacts between Node, Rust/WASM, Python, and Java. Feature What it describes Why it helps path_len Length of the request path. Unusually long probing paths. kw_hits Matches against malicious keywords. Known probing patterns within a path. resp_time Response duration in seconds. Behavior that differs from the normal timing distribution. status_idx An encoded response-status category. Response outcomes without treating status codes as continuous measurements. burst_count Requests associated with the client in the burst window. Rapid repeated activity. total_404 Not-found responses in the relevant per-client history. Repeated discovery of nonexistent routes. The feature order is part of the model contract. A trainer and scorer must agree on the order, status mapping, time units, and window semantics. Summary fields ending in _ms use milliseconds; the feature vector uses seconds. Sharing feature names alone does not make every model artifact interchangeable. Optional WASM execution wasmAdapter.js loads available Rust-backed primitives and converts JavaScript inputs into the WASM representation. The middleware still decides which checks apply, what to log, and when to reject a request. If initialization or conversion is unsuitable, JavaScript implementations remain available. Crossing the binding boundary has a fixed conversion cost. Large feature batches and forest workloads can benefit; small object-heavy calls may be faster in JavaScript. WASM is a computation backend, not a separate HTTP firewall service. Worked example: one denied request A nonexempt request with valid headers reaches the rate limiter. If its shared or local window exceeds the configured maximum, the middleware marks the denial, sends 429 unless a flood or blocklist path determines another status, and returns. The application handler does not run. Logging can still observe the completed denial because its hook was attached earlier. System overview explains the common layers; operations covers CLI, training, and runtime configuration. Trace the implementation Follow these files in the monorepo to connect the architecture to the code: js/index.js js/lib/wafMiddleware.js js/lib/pathRules.js js/lib/pathManifest.js js/lib/sourceAst.js js/lib/rateLimiter.js js/lib/anomalyDetector.js js/lib/wasmAdapter.js

title: Node.js Operations
text: Node.js Operations Current Node source and framework support The source candidate is aiwaf 1.1.5 with the declared aiwaf-wasm ^0.2.5 dependency. Publish the matching WASM companion first. The native request engine still requires explicit registration and awaits initialization; a missing native API fails startup. Legacy adapters keep their separate configuration and execution path. Offline training now uses WASM receipts to prevent handled historical requests from extending or recreating blocks after expiry or manual removal. Models still fit on history; enforcement uses fresh requests. Preserve node_training_evidence.json in the blocklist data directory, or set AIWAF_TRAINING_STATE_DIR to a durable shared directory. Invalid timestamps are excluded. Missing WASM APIs, corrupt receipts, and storage failures make training fail visibly. A crashed trainer can leave node_training_evidence.lock ; confirm it has stopped before removing that lock directory. Block and receipt writes are separate, so a crash between them can require recovery. The current reference tests use Node 22.18.0 , Express 4, Fastify 5, and NestJS 11. These are tested configurations, not a claim that every framework version is supported. Use the framework and adapter matching your application. Next.js examples require Node API request/response objects; Edge middleware is not supported by this adapter. Legacy blocklist request checks and listing are read-only. Explicit database cleanup checks expiry in the DELETE statement; CSV cleanup reads current rows under the same cross-process lock used by blocklist writes. A crash can leave <blocklist CSV path>.lock ; confirm its writer has stopped before removing that directory. Lock acquisition fails after 60 seconds. Restart all old writers when upgrading. These fixes do not make the explicit native engine's per-worker state distributed. For source development, use the committed lockfile with npm ci , run the coverage and real native checks, and audit the complete tree with npm audit . Read dependency versions and verification and native migration . How AIWAF works: system architecture Legacy CLI and training from source The commands in this section operate on legacy Node stores. They do not import or manage the native engine's dedicated CSV event files. cd js AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG=/path/to/access.log npm run train npm run aiwaf -- status npm run aiwaf -- list blocklist npm run aiwaf -- add blocklist 203.0.113.9 "manual block" npm run aiwaf -- add ip-exemption 203.0.113.10 "trusted monitor" npm run aiwaf -- geo summary npm run aiwaf -- model info npm run aiwaf -- export aiwaf-export.json Use Redis or another shared cache for consistent rate limiting across multiple Node processes. Without shared state, the in-memory fallback is process-local. The npm run commands above use the package scripts in the monorepo's js/ directory. In an application that installed the package, use the installed binary, for example npx aiwaf status or npx aiwaf --help . Configuration Area Important options Middleware AIWAF_MIDDLEWARES , AIWAF_DISABLE_MIDDLEWARES , AIWAF_PATH_RULES Rate limiting WINDOW_SEC , MAX_REQ , FLOOD_REQ , cache Headers AIWAF_HEADER_VALIDATION , AIWAF_REQUIRED_HEADERS , AIWAF_HEADER_QUALITY_MIN_SCORE Methods AIWAF_METHOD_POLICY_ENABLED , AIWAF_ALLOWED_METHODS Keywords staticKeywords , AIWAF_ENABLE_KEYWORD_LEARNING , AIWAF_DYNAMIC_TOP_N Honeypot HONEYPOT_FIELD , timing settings GeoIP AIWAF_GEO_BLOCK_ENABLED , AIWAF_GEO_BLOCK_COUNTRIES , AIWAF_GEO_ALLOW_COUNTRIES Models AIWAF_MODEL_STORAGE , AIWAF_MODEL_PATH , AIWAF_MODEL_CACHE_KEY Logging AIWAF_MIDDLEWARE_LOGGING , AIWAF_MIDDLEWARE_LOG_PATH , DB/CSV options WASM AIWAF_WASM_VALIDATION , AIWAF_WASM_VALIDATE_RECENT AIWAF loads aiwaf-wasm when available and falls back to the JavaScript implementation when WASM initialization or conversion is not worthwhile. Small, object-heavy operations can be faster in JavaScript because crossing the JS/WASM boundary and serializing objects has a fixed cost. WASM is most useful for sufficiently large feature batches and model scoring workloads. Development checks Run from the monorepo root: npm ci --prefix js npm test --prefix js python aiwaf_test.py --js-only python aiwaf_test.py --wasm-only Packaging The package manifest is js/package.json ; the CLI entry is js/bin/aiwaf.js . Release tags use js-v<version> and the npm-publish.yml workflow. The root README and LICENSE are staged into package artifacts by release automation. Request parsing and cache failures For custom Node HTTP servers or middleware registered before a framework parser, call aiwaf.bodyParser() before AIWAF and before forwarding requests. It parses JSON and URL-encoded bodies, retains original forwarding bytes, and rejects oversized bodies (default 64 KiB). Fastify/Hapi integrations must enforce AIWAF after body parsing and before their proxy handler. Redis rate-cache failures return generic HTTP 503. AIWAF_RATE_CACHE_FAILURE_MODE defaults to 'closed' ; explicitly choosing 'open' allows requests during cache failures. The new filesystem CSV transactions and retained training handles are Python/PyO3 capabilities; installing WASM does not migrate Node middleware/storage to that implementation. Native deployment and benchmarking Native mode: Node source candidate aiwaf 1.1.5 declares aiwaf-wasm ^0.2.5 . Explicit native registration validates NativeRequestPipeline at startup; missing or incompatible support is an error. There is no JavaScript policy fallback for this engine. Installing the dependency does not switch an existing legacy middleware chain. Build/install the matching WASM companion first, await initialization, verify diagnostics().native and diagnostics().model, and test normal routes, unknown PHP paths and nested SQL bodies. Use setModel(model) to replace the fitted Rust snapshot or restart. The legacy trainer/log stores are separate from the native event files; do not assume an automatic import. Run npm run test:native from js/ in the source checkout. node scripts/benchmark_js_pipeline.js compares full HTTP requests against bare Express, with AI off/on and actual inference counters. Server samples include synchronous finalization/logging, and overhead subtracts the framework-only baseline. Legacy SQLite/JSONL and native Rust/CSV have different persistence semantics, so comparisons are integration results rather than pure language speedups. Stop traffic and wait for in-flight responses before close(). Model/rate/honeypot/history state is local; persisted blocks/keywords only reload on reconstruction. Publication must make the compatible WASM API available before users enable native mode. Read the native lifecycle , configuration , deployment and measurements , and migration . Measured Node request overhead Windows x64, Node v22.18.0, Express 4.22.1, built WASM 0.2.2. Three alternating runs of 300 requests per mode, one keep-alive client. 80% GET / 20% JSON POST with 30 fields; 1,000 blocklist entries; all eight stages selected; memory rate/form state. Native AI uses a seeded 100-tree forest fitted to 200 rows, with one inference per measured/warm-up request verified by counters. Mode Server processing Added overhead Express only 0.37 ms 0.00 ms Legacy, AI off 3.86 ms 3.48 ms Native, AI off 0.60 ms 0.22 ms Native, AI on 0.64 ms 0.27 ms Server samples include synchronous finalization and immediate logging. Overhead subtracts the matched bare Express baseline; figures are medians of per-run means. Legacy uses SQLite policy lookups and one immediate JSONL append; native uses Rust state and one immediate CSV append. These stores/policies have different persistence semantics, so this is an integration comparison, not a pure Rust-versus-JavaScript equivalence test. GeoIP is an unknown-country fixture, not a real database lookup. Synthetic local latency does not establish production throughput or latency. Native execution and actual inference counters were verified; all 3,600 measured requests returned 200. Protected SQL/PHP probes returned 403. Reproduce from the source checkout with scripts/benchmark_js_pipeline.js . Dependency security and reproducible checks The source lockfile uses Jest 30.5.2, Fastify 5.12.7, and patched NestJS 11 dependencies (the validated install resolved 11.2.7). The direct glob dependency is 13.0.6. Targeted overrides update qs and the NYC loader's YAML dependency; old global parser overrides have been removed. Framework packages in devDependencies support adapter testing; they do not select the framework for an installed application. cd js npm ci npm audit npm run test:coverage npm run test:wasm npm run test:native The repository's Jest tests use generated CommonJS WASM bindings through AIWAF_NATIVE_TEST_MODULE . Release CI builds that fixture from rust/crates/aiwaf_wasm and runs real installed-WASM checks separately. Jest also transforms the ESM cookie dependency used by Fastify's injection client so the suite works on Node 22. Earlier dependency validation on 13 October 2026 passed 227 tests across 63 suites, with coverage thresholds met, plus real WASM and native framework transport checks. npm ci and the full npm audit reported zero known vulnerabilities for that lockfile. The release workflow audits production and development dependencies. Rerun the audit after dependency changes; this result describes the tested tree and advisory database at that time. Upstream deprecation warnings remain for SQLite's prebuild-install and coverage tooling's glob 10 dependency. Deprecation notices and blocked optional install scripts are separate from audit findings. The repository permits SQLite's install script; the tested installation did not require enabling every optional postinstall script. The latency figures above were measured before this dependency update. They have not been remeasured with the patched tree. October 2026 release upgrade The prepared source versions are Python 1.1.6 , Rust/Python 0.2.5 , Node.js 1.1.4 , WASM 0.2.4 , and Java 1.3.4 . These are source targets; verify registry availability before installing. Python requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.5 , including the TrainingEvidence API. Node offline training requires the matching WASM receipt API. Back up policies, logs, models, and training evidence. Use the same absolute data and evidence directories for application workers and CLI trainers. Install the matching native companion before upgrading its host package: Rust before Python, WASM before Node. Preserve training_evidence.json and node_training_evidence.json across expiry, unblocking, restarts, and log rotation. Stop older file writers and restart all workers on the new code. Mixing old unlocked writers with new writers can still lose updates. In staging, train twice on identical logs, then verify handled evidence does not recreate a removed or expired block. Add genuinely fresh requests and confirm they must independently satisfy the enforcement threshold. Verify that listing and expiry checks preserve concurrently refreshed blocks and unrelated IPs. Check the raw expiry and backend location if entries disappear unexpectedly. Java CSV and file storage Java 1.3.4 reloads current storage under a shared JVM and OS sidecar lock for each operation. Reads filter expiry without rewriting disk; mutations preserve other instances' updates and report persistence failures. This adds file I/O. Java model training still does not add blocklist entries. Rate buckets and other per-engine memory state retain their existing isolation. Lock recovery Python training uses an OS file lock; Java CSV/file OS locks also release on process exit. Keep their stable sidecar lock files in place while workers run. Node uses lock directories for training and legacy CSV mutations; a crash can leave them behind. Confirm the owning process has stopped before removing a Node lock directory. Do not delete training receipts to clear a lock: doing so loses handled-evidence history. Release checks Local validation passed 247 Node tests across 67 suites with the coverage gate, 215 Java tests with 3 skips, and 38 Rust/WASM native tests. After the native dependency bump, 11 affected Python packaging tests passed through the appropriate Django and pytest runners. These checks do not replace full release CI, dependency audits, signing, or operating-system wheel builds. Build Linux/macOS Rust wheels using the release matrix; the local bundle contains a Windows x86-64 wheel. For release maintainers: publish the WASM companion, refresh the Node lockfile from the registry to record its actual integrity, then run npm ci and the native integration checks. Do not substitute an older native dependency to satisfy a stale packaging test. See the changelog .

How AIWAF works: system architecture Protect an AdonisJS application, confirm the adapter runs before its handler, and decide how routes and state should be managed. Before you begin An existing AdonisJS application with a working route and middleware registry. The file below defines a middleware class; it must also be registered in your application. Use a Node.js version supported by your framework and dependency lockfile. For an existing application, confirm that its ordinary routes work before integrating AIWAF. 1. Install the adapter and dependencies npm install aiwaf Install the framework dependencies used by your existing application. The Node middleware package is aiwaf ; source code and package scripts live in the monorepo's js/ directory. 2. Register the adapter app/middleware/aiwaf_middleware.ts The adapter returns an asynchronous (ctx, next) function. Wrap it in an Adonis middleware class and register that class through your application's middleware configuration: import aiwaf from 'aiwaf'; const protect = aiwaf.adonis({ AIWAF_MIDDLEWARES: ['auto'] }); export default class AiwafMiddleware { async handle(ctx, next) { return protect(ctx, next); } } How this registration works Register this class in the generated server/router middleware registry for your Adonis version and scope it to the intended routes. Merely creating the file does not run it. Preserve the body parser before checks needing parsed input. auto selects checks based on application signals; it is not a fixed promise that every check runs. Review the Node request lifecycle and configuration reference when choosing checks. 3. Run and verify the integration node ace serve --watch Open http://127.0.0.1:3333/ in a browser. The example handler returns {"protected": true} ; existing NestJS/Adonis/Sails routes return their own handler response. This proves reachability, so also test an intended rejection on a non-exempt route before rollout. A plain curl client can fail header checks when they are selected. Inspect the actual response and logs, route policy, and observed client address. A private client or exempt path may bypass enforcement. See the controlled allow/throttle exercise for what an enforcement test should establish. Place body parsing before checks that need parsed fields. Follow the middleware registration API for your Adonis version. 4. Discover routes and review policy Generate a manifest after the application's routes are registered. Express applications can call aiwaf.generateExpressManifest(app, '.aiwaf/paths.json') . Other adapters expose aiwaf.generateFrameworkManifest(framework, app, outputPath, options) with framework-specific route extraction. For a route list stored in routes.json , use the installed CLI: npx aiwaf manifest --framework adonis --routes routes.json --output .aiwaf/paths.json Review the resulting manifest and repeat generation when routes change. Manifest generation complements AIWAF_MIDDLEWARES: ['auto'] and explicit AIWAF_PATH_RULES overrides. Operate the installed package npx aiwaf --help npx aiwaf status npx aiwaf list blocklist npx aiwaf model info For offline training from a source checkout: cd aiwaf/js AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG=/path/to/access.log npm run train PowerShell users can set $env:AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG = '/path/to/access.log' before npm run train . Application installs do not inherit the package's npm scripts; use the installed CLI or the source checkout as appropriate. Verify and deploy Test normal routes, narrowly scoped exemptions, configured header policy, and rate-limit behavior in staging. Persist logs and model artifacts and schedule training after traffic volume thresholds are met. In-memory enforcement is process-local; use Redis or another shared cache when rate limits must span workers. Choose a runtime Next: understand Node architecture Select the native WASM engine Native mode: Node source candidate aiwaf 1.1.5 declares aiwaf-wasm ^0.2.5 . Explicit native registration validates NativeRequestPipeline at startup; missing or incompatible support is an error. There is no JavaScript policy fallback for this engine. Installing the dependency does not switch an existing legacy middleware chain. Select this adapter with { AIWAF_NATIVE_PIPELINE: { dataDir: "aiwaf_native_data", profile: { min_form_time: 1.0 } } } . This is a separate lowercase profile: do not mix legacy constructor options, PATH_RULES, cache or custom stores. Fastify/Hapi await startup during registration. Koa/Adonis/Next wrappers expose .ready and Nest exposes static .ready; await it before serving, and close the resolved native handle after responses complete. Bounded framework body parsing must precede parsed-body checks. Read the native lifecycle , configuration , deployment and measurements , and migration .

title: Upgrade and Migration Guide
text: Upgrade and Migration Guide All maintained packages use the AIWAF monorepo . Each package releases independently. Compare the installed version, source manifest, and release notes for your runtime before upgrading; source versions are not confirmation that a registry release exists. Upgrade sequence Record installed versions, enabled middleware, exemptions, configuration, state backend, model path, and proxy behavior. Back up persisted state, configuration, and models. Upgrade one runtime in staging using its package manager or build from a reviewed source revision. Preserve the matching dependency lockfiles. Apply package-name and configuration changes below. Regenerate manifests from the live application after its routes are registered. Migrate blocklist state with the runtime's supported command; inspect counts, expiry, reasons, and exemptions afterward. Regenerate unsupported models with the current trainer. Verify schema, feature order, output location, and load diagnostics. Test normal public traffic, intentional blocks, rate boundaries, intended exemptions, and actual response logging. Test across workers when state is shared. Deploy code, configuration, and compatible state/models together. Reload workers and repeat checks. Keep a compatible rollback snapshot. Node.js package name The npm middleware package is now aiwaf . Replace the old dependency and imports; regenerate the lockfile and test every adapter entrypoint your application uses. npm uninstall aiwaf-js npm install aiwaf const aiwaf = require('aiwaf'); app.use(aiwaf({ AIWAF_MIDDLEWARES: ['all'] })); aiwaf-wasm remains a separate package. Installing it does not replace Node framework middleware. Check normalized aliases and defaults in the configuration reference before moving settings between versions. Python reputation and blocklist data Python 1.0.7 introduced weighted reputation, progressive temporary blocking, expiry, and richer metadata. Legacy blocklist compatibility is backend-aware, including CSV schema detection and conversion of imported permanent blocks. Use the same checkout, environment, and backend configuration as your application: aiwaf blocklist migrate When multiple frameworks are installed, choose an explicit prefix such as aiwaf flask --help or aiwaf fastapi --help . --framework and --app are route-discovery options for aiwaf init . Do not manually reinterpret old CSV columns or assume historical permanent blocks retain identical enforcement semantics. Back up first and compare the resulting entries. Python models and Rust acceleration Persisted Python runtime models are JSON. Pickle, joblib, and executable Python-object artifacts are unsupported; use representative logs and the current trainer to create a new model. Check minimum log thresholds rather than forcing production training on a tiny sample. Python 1.1.8 requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.7 ; the Rust extra remains an installation alias. The explicit native request engine validates its required APIs at startup. Installing the companion does not replace an existing legacy middleware chain. Upgrade both packages in the deployed interpreter and verify the real adapter after restarting workers. python -m pip install --upgrade 'aiwaf[flask,rust]' # Use the extra matching your application. aiwaf flask train --help aiwaf flask model --help Route manifests and import targets aiwaf init --framework flask --app app:app aiwaf init --framework flask --app app:create_app aiwaf init --framework fastapi --app app:app aiwaf init --framework django --settings project.settings --app app.py is invalid. The target must be a module and application object/factory. Run discovery in the application's environment; it imports the application. Do not carry a stale manifest across route changes. Java 1.2 and 1.3 changes Java 1.2 adds scoped per-engine storage, distributed Redis enforcement state, Spring Boot live route/annotation discovery, JSON/environment configuration, native MaxMind lookup, and updated reputation behavior. Remove the old requirement for an external mmdblookup executable. Review default private-address exemptions and manifest loading. Java 1.3 adds bounded Redis connection/socket/pool waits, fail-open/fail-closed policy, diagnostics, and state-schema compatibility guards. It supports standalone Redis and rejects Sentinel/Cluster modes. Before a rolling upgrade, test old/new instances with the intended namespace and schema. Do not bypass compatibility guards or point unrelated services at one prefix. Review legacy model feature schema against the current six-feature pipeline; retrain or use an explicit supported importer when required. Artifacts are not generally interchangeable between languages. Spring Boot applications should use the ordered filter once, rather than adding an independent interceptor as a second enforcement layer. Rollback and release notes Restore compatible code, configuration, state, and model artifacts together. Avoid reverting code while leaving a newer incompatible state schema. Repeat public-client and shared-worker checks after reload. See the upstream changelog , Python operations , Node operations , and Java operations for runtime commands. Python 1.1.2 and Rust 0.2.2 migration Back up policy CSV files, logs, route manifests, and JSON model artifacts. Install matching Python/framework and Rust extras in the interpreter used by WSGI/ASGI; restart workers after installation. Run scripts/check_native_csv_runtime.py from the source checkout in the deployment environment. Verify allowed routes, blocked probes, external policy updates, CSV logging, and rate-cache behavior across workers. CSV rate buckets are explicit, not selected by CSV blocklist storage. Train with representative logs. CSV/gzip ingestion now streams directly; custom parsers retain their compatibility path. Reload FastAPI anomaly middleware or restart after producing a new model. Native policy updates are atomic under filesystem locks. Keep compatible schemas in rolling upgrades; older Python writers on Windows do not provide equivalent cross-process locking. Avoid concurrent whole-file replacement. Model schemas, status mapping, timestamp semantics, and seconds/milliseconds units must remain compatible. Redis configuration errors no longer silently select process memory in Flask. Runtime Redis rate-cache failures return generic HTTP 503 in Python. Check Redis connectivity/configuration before rollout. Native CSV rate buckets also return 503 when native support is unavailable. Python 1.1.8 / Rust 0.2.7 migration Release candidate: this page documents Python 1.1.8 and Rust/Python 0.2.7 in the current source checkout. Source versions do not establish registry availability. Python 1.1.8 requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.7 ; framework dependencies remain extras. Install the explicit native adapter instead of the existing AIWAF middleware chain. Installing the required Rust dependency does not automatically switch existing applications to this pipeline. Legacy adapters remain available for custom stores and hooks; their configuration and fallback behavior are separate. Back up compatible policy CSVs, request logs and trained model artifacts. Install the release candidate from the source checkout or, once published, the matching framework extra. Verify the deployed interpreter imports aiwaf_rust.NativeCSVPipeline and restart workers. Replace the existing AIWAF chain with exactly one native framework adapter. Retain application session/authentication middleware and set up adapter authentication facts. Translate supported settings into the dedicated lowercase profile. Do not copy uppercase or nested legacy dictionaries. Choose explicit rate/honeypot worker-sharing semantics. Pass a trained Rust model explicitly if inference is required. Confirm model activation; otherwise history/learning operate without model-based blocking. Verify normal routes, unknown paths, SQL/PHP rejection, method/header checks, decorator exemptions, logs, state updates and cross-worker timing. Benchmark against the same framework-only handler before rollout. Keep the legacy adapters if you need unsupported Redis, ORM/custom stores or custom policy hooks. There is no automatic fallback from the new engine. Restore compatible configuration, code and state together on rollback; switching timing backends does not migrate timestamps. Continue with the request lifecycle , the native profile , migration , and performance and deployment . Migrate Node to the native engine Native mode: Node source candidate aiwaf 1.1.4 declares aiwaf-wasm ^0.2.4 . Explicit native registration validates NativeRequestPipeline at startup; missing or incompatible support is an error. There is no JavaScript policy fallback for this engine. Installing the dependency does not switch an existing legacy middleware chain. Back up legacy configuration, logs, policies and compatible model artifacts. Build/install the matching companion and use one native adapter instead of the old chain. Translate supported configuration to the lowercase profile; keep the legacy adapter for Redis, custom database stores or unsupported hooks. Install bounded parsers and route metadata before checks; supply country/authentication/route facts. Choose separate data/log files per worker and account for local counters/timing/history. Legacy state is not migrated automatically. Load a compatible Rust model explicitly, then verify allowed requests, unknown paths, nested payload rejection, model inference and logs. Read the native lifecycle , configuration , deployment and measurements , and migration . Shared Python policy CSV migration Source release change: Flask, FastAPI, Django CSV mode, and the native Rust pipeline now use the same five policy CSV schemas. FastAPI CSV configuration should use storage.backend = "csv" and storage.data_dir = "/absolute/path/aiwaf_data" . Use the same absolute directory for the application and CLI. Memory, JSON, database, and Django ORM modes retain their existing behavior. Stop old workers and back up state before upgrading. Startup imports runtime_store.csv in the chosen directory. The old default aiwaf_data.csv is imported into the adjoining project aiwaf_data directory. Custom legacy storage.file_path values remain accepted: /path/custom.csv maps to /path/custom/ ; runtime_store.csv maps to its parent. Specify data_dir to choose a different destination. Verify blocks, expiry times, exemptions, keywords, country lists, and path exemptions. Existing canonical policy wins conflicts. Original legacy sources remain intact; canonical files are backed up before import, and completion markers prevent replay after removals. Invalid legacy input fails startup. Repair it and restart to retry an incomplete import. Future writes to a completed legacy source are not imported again. Keyword frequencies and non-policy history remain in runtime_metadata.csv . Enforcement reads blacklist.csv , whitelist.csv , keywords.csv , geo_blocked_countries.csv , and path_exemptions.csv . Restore compatible code and its original legacy state together for rollback. Node dependency security upgrade Update both js/package.json and its lockfile, then use npm ci . Current source tests use Jest 30, Fastify 5, and patched NestJS 11. Older broad overrides for body parsers and route-pattern parsers are removed so newer framework dependencies use compatible APIs. Test the adapter matching the application's framework after updating its own dependency tree. The Node source version is 1.1.4; dependency changes do not imply publication. The full audit was clean on 13 October 2026. Keep development dependencies in the audit and run coverage, real WASM, and native transport checks. Native Node event stores still require a separate migration decision; Python's automatic runtime CSV import does not apply to Node. Read the reproducible commands and validation scope . October 2026 release upgrade The prepared source versions are Python 1.1.6 , Rust/Python 0.2.5 , Node.js 1.1.4 , WASM 0.2.4 , and Java 1.3.4 . These are source targets; verify registry availability before installing. Python requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.5 , including the TrainingEvidence API. Node offline training requires the matching WASM receipt API. Back up policies, logs, models, and training evidence. Use the same absolute data and evidence directories for application workers and CLI trainers. Install the matching native companion before upgrading its host package: Rust before Python, WASM before Node. Preserve training_evidence.json and node_training_evidence.json across expiry, unblocking, restarts, and log rotation. Stop older file writers and restart all workers on the new code. Mixing old unlocked writers with new writers can still lose updates. In staging, train twice on identical logs, then verify handled evidence does not recreate a removed or expired block. Add genuinely fresh requests and confirm they must independently satisfy the enforcement threshold. Verify that listing and expiry checks preserve concurrently refreshed blocks and unrelated IPs. Check the raw expiry and backend location if entries disappear unexpectedly. Java CSV and file storage Java 1.3.4 reloads current storage under a shared JVM and OS sidecar lock for each operation. Reads filter expiry without rewriting disk; mutations preserve other instances' updates and report persistence failures. This adds file I/O. Java model training still does not add blocklist entries. Rate buckets and other per-engine memory state retain their existing isolation. Lock recovery Python training uses an OS file lock; Java CSV/file OS locks also release on process exit. Keep their stable sidecar lock files in place while workers run. Node uses lock directories for training and legacy CSV mutations; a crash can leave them behind. Confirm the owning process has stopped before removing a Node lock directory. Do not delete training receipts to clear a lock: doing so loses handled-evidence history. Release checks Local validation passed 247 Node tests across 67 suites with the coverage gate, 215 Java tests with 3 skips, and 38 Rust/WASM native tests. After the native dependency bump, 11 affected Python packaging tests passed through the appropriate Django and pytest runners. These checks do not replace full release CI, dependency audits, signing, or operating-system wheel builds. Build Linux/macOS Rust wheels using the release matrix; the local bundle contains a Windows x86-64 wheel. For release maintainers: publish the WASM companion, refresh the Node lockfile from the registry to record its actual integrity, then run npm ci and the native integration checks. Do not substitute an older native dependency to satisfy a stale packaging test. See the changelog .

title: AIWAF-PHP Architecture Deep Dive
text: Core Design AIWAF-PHP Architecture Deep Dive How AIWAF works: system architecture Legacy PHP reference. The current monorepo does not contain a PHP package or PHP release workflow. These historical examples have not been validated against the current repo. Use the current Python, Node.js, Java, or Rust/WASM guides for new integrations. 1-4. Purpose, Snapshot, Structure, Architecture Package: aayushgauba/aiwaf , Composer library, PHP >=7.4 . Primary runtime entry: AIWAF::protect() ; training entry: cli/detect_and_train.php . Top-level focus: src/ , src/Core/ , src/Adapters/ , src/RateLimit/ , resources/ , tests/ . Design traits: defense-in-depth, exemption-first, conservative AI guardrails, flexible persistence backends. 5. Runtime Entry And Integration Surface Primary API ( src/AIWAF.php ) AIWAF::protect() executes per-request security controls. AIWAF::setPathExistsResolver() enables route-awareness for framework integrations. AIWAF::setMiddlewareDecisionResolver() supports custom middleware gating logic. AIWAF::getLastTrainingTelemetry() exposes latest trainer telemetry snapshot. Typical Bootstrap Load Composer autoload. Initialize selected rate-limit adapter. Call AIWAF::protect() early in front-controller lifecycle. 6. Request Protection Flow ( AIWAF::protect ) Build runtime config via Config::toRuntimeConfig() . Configure rate limiter via configureRateLimiter() (auto-detects db, apcu, redis, or falls back to memory). Resolve request identity ( ip , path ). Exemption short-circuit (skips remaining checks if IP or Path is exempt via configurations or CIDR matches). Method validation (ensures request method is allowed). Header validation (evaluates trust_legitimate_bots , custom_suspicious_patterns , and quality_threshold ). Blocked-IP enforcement. Geo policy checks (compares IP against allow/block countries). AI Anomaly Scoring: Extracts an 8-dimensional feature vector: strlen($path) DynamicKeywordManager::detect($path) 0.5 (baseline structural complexity) Status code anomaly ( 1 if 404/500, else 0 ) Reserved ( 0 ) Reserved ( 0 ) Honeypot trigger ( isset($_POST['aiwaf_honeytrap']) ? 1 : 0 ) UUID tamper check ( UUIDTamperProtector::isSuspicious($path) ? 1 : 0 ) Scores the vector against forest_model.json . If score exceeds threshold, it runs a post-prediction guard ensuring at least one strong signal (e.g., keyword hits ≥ 2.0 or direct honeypot/UUID triggers) before blocking. Rate-limit enforcement (checks max_requests per window_seconds ). Dynamic keyword checks. UUID tamper checks. Honeypot checks (evaluates $_POST payloads). Block responses use 403 for deny cases and 429 for rate-limit violations. AST Static Analysis ( src/Core/ApiDetection.php ) PHP dynamically analyzes controller logic during startup using Abstract Syntax Trees to determine endpoint intent (API vs. Form vs. Auth). This is heavily utilized when native framework routes don't strictly typehint their return models. Parsing: Uses nikic/php-parser ( PhpParser\ParserFactory ) to construct an AST directly from the controller's source file, using reflection ( ReflectionMethod , ReflectionFunction ) to locate the exact start and end lines of the closure or method. Traversal: A custom NodeVisitorAbstract traverses the statements strictly within the bounded line numbers. Call Inspection: Inspects MethodCall , FuncCall , and StaticCall nodes. Increases API confidence if it detects json , json_encode , JsonResponse , or jsonify . Increases Form confidence if it detects view , render , redirect , back , or render_template . Object Instantiation: Inspects New_ nodes. Instantiating JsonResponse yields a high API score. Payload Type: Scans for post , all , input , or file method calls on request objects to flag requestBody = true and classify the expected payload. Path Generation and Auto Middleware ( MiddlewarePlan.php ) AIWAF for PHP includes intelligent path generation and middleware auto-negotiation to dynamically optimize the protection pipeline per endpoint: Route Classification ( PathManifest::classifyRoute ): The manifest generator infers the primary intent of any given route, categorizing paths as api , form , admin , upload , static , or auth . Auto Middleware Planning: Based on the route classification, the engine automatically toggles specific middlewares on or off. For example: API Endpoints: Disables HTML Honeypots, enforces strict JSON payload validation, and allocates a high rate-limit ceiling (120 req/min). Form Endpoints: Enables Honeypot validation, sets strict rate limits (30 req/min), and enforces POST payload sizes. Static Assets: Automatically disables AI Anomaly scoring, Honeypots, and Header Validation to drastically reduce CPU overhead on /static/ or .png routes. Config Sentinels: If requested_middlewares is set to ['auto'] , MiddlewarePlan::planEnabledMiddlewares() dynamically strips out unnecessary middlewares (e.g., completely unloading uuid_tamper if no UUIDs exist, or disabling geo_block if the MMDB isn't configured). Deep Dive: Core Functions and Methods A reference of the core internal functions powering the PHP AIWAF engine. Module / Class Function / Method Description AIWAF.php AIWAF protect() The primary execution gate. Iterates through the resolved middleware plan, terminating the request with a 403 or 429 payload if any middleware rejects. PathManifest.php PathManifest classifyRoute($path, $methods) Matches standard heuristic signatures (e.g., /api/* or /login ) and combines them with AST outputs to bin the route type. ApiDetection.php RouteVisitor enterNode(Node $node) Implements PhpParser\NodeVisitorAbstract to inspect method calls like json() or validate() to build confidence scores for API intents. MiddlewarePlan.php MiddlewarePlan resolve($path, $category) Yields the final array of active middlewares. Trims expensive operations (like HTML honing) when $category === 'api' . detect_and_train.php (CLI Script) extractFeatures($logLine) Parses a line of access logs into the 6-dimension float array needed for training the Isolation Forest. detect_and_train.php (CLI Script) calculateThresholds() Evaluates historical traffic baselines to automatically tune max_req and flood_req dynamically. 7. Core Modules Responsibility Map src/ AIWAF.php , Config.php , Utils.php RateLimiter.php , IPBlocker.php DynamicKeywordManager.php , UUIDTamperProtector.php , HoneypotChecker.php FeatureExtractor.php , IsolationForest.php , Logger.php src/Core/ RuntimeConfig.php , HeaderValidation.php , GeoIP.php , Exemptions.php Logs.php , Training.php , TrainingLogic.php StorageOps.php , StorageCsvImpl.php , StorageSchema.php , BlocklistManager.php Rate-Limit Layers Adapters in src/Adapters/ bridge runtime usage. Drivers in src/RateLimit/ provide backend-specific persistence behavior. 8-9. Storage, Artifacts, Training Lifecycle Artifacts (default under resources/ ) blocked_ips.json , dynamic_keywords.json , request_features.csv , forest_model.json . php setup.php ensures required baseline files exist. Training Pipeline ( AIWAF::detectAndTrain ) The training pipeline executes robust anomaly detection and keyword learning strategies via CLI ( php cli/detect_and_train.php ): Source Processing: Reads from AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG , automatically parsing rotated and gzipped logs via Logs::readRotatedLogs . Feature Extraction: Capable of parallelized feature extraction via FeatureExtractor::pythonFeaturesBatched if Python is available (managed by AIWAF_PYTHON_PARALLEL_WORKERS ). Training Matrix: Extracted per request for the IsolationForest (configured with 200 trees, 32 sample size). The matrix maps 6 dimensions: path_len kw_hits resp_time status_idx burst_count total_404 Anomaly Evaluation: Evaluates the matrix against the model using AIWAF_AI_ANOMALY_THRESHOLD . Identifies anomalous IPs and runs a strict conservative check: keeps burst-only traffic with no suspicious footprint unblocked. Blocks only if: average keyword hits ≥ 2.0, max 404s ≥ 10.0, average burst ≥ 15.0, or total requests ≥ 100. Keyword Learning: Extracts suspicious path segments into the dynamic keyword store, skipping paths that match exempt_paths or known_paths . Telemetry Includes line counts, parse failures, feature rows keyword candidate/learned counts anomalous/blocked IP totals and top-country summaries

Prerequisites 2.1 Runtime PHP >= 7.4 Composer Optional ext-redis when using Redis adapter/driver 2.2 System dependencies Writable filesystem for resources/ runtime artifacts. Access to application/proxy logs for training ( AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG ). 2.3 Recommended for production Persistent storage for runtime artifacts and model files. Scheduled training runs ( php cli/detect_and_train.php ). Known route/path hints configured to reduce false positives. 3. Installation Paths # Application install composer require aayushgauba/aiwaf # Local development in this repository composer install # Initialize runtime resources php setup.php 4. Core Configuration Concepts AIWAF-PHP can be configured through static config, runtime config, and env mapping in RuntimeConfig::loadFromEnvironment() . Header validation: AIWAF_HEADER_VALIDATION_ENABLED , AIWAF_HEADER_BLOCK_SUSPICIOUS , AIWAF_HEADER_QUALITY_THRESHOLD , AIWAF_HEADER_EXEMPT_PATHS Rate limiting: AIWAF_RATE_LIMITING_ENABLED , AIWAF_RATE_MAX_REQUESTS , AIWAF_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS , AIWAF_EXEMPT_IPS Detection toggles: IP/keyword, honeypot, AI anomaly, UUID tamper toggles Geo policy: allow/block countries Training controls: access log, thresholds, force/disable flags, anomaly threshold, known paths 5. Auto Middleware & Path Manifest Setup AIWAF-PHP can automatically tune your middleware protections based on your application's routing structure. By generating a Path Manifest, AIWAF categorizes your endpoints (e.g., API vs HTML Form) and automatically disables unnecessary middlewares (like Honeypots for APIs) and enforces strict rate limits where appropriate. # Generate the path manifest automatically php cli/detect_and_train.php --generate-manifest At startup, AIWAF reads the manifest from .aiwaf/paths.json to auto-configure the execution chain. If you prefer fine-grained manual control over your middleware stack rather than relying on auto-generation, proceed to the framework-specific "All Middlewares" manual setup sections below. 6. Framework Setup (All Middlewares) Laravel Use patterns under examples/laravel/ (service provider + train command). AIWAF::setPathExistsResolver(function (string $path): bool { $candidate = '/' . ltrim((string) strtok($path, '?'), '/'); foreach (Route::getRoutes() as $route) { $uri = '/' . ltrim($route->uri(), '/'); if ($candidate === $uri || strpos($candidate, $uri . '/') === 0) { return true; } } return false; }); 8. Storage Setup and Backend Choices 7.1 Default behavior Core runtime artifacts are file-backed under resources/ . php setup.php ensures base files exist. 7.2 Key artifact files resources/blocked_ips.json resources/dynamic_keywords.json resources/request_features.csv resources/forest_model.json 7.3 Rate-limit adapter/backend options In-memory adapter APCu adapter Redis adapter DB adapter 9. Training Setup 8.1 Configure training log source # Linux/macOS export AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG=/var/log/nginx/access.log # PowerShell $env:AIWAF_ACCESS_LOG = "C:\path\to\access.log" 8.2 Run training php cli/detect_and_train.php 8.3 Useful training env examples AIWAF_MIN_TRAIN_LOGS=50 AIWAF_MIN_AI_LOGS=10000 AIWAF_FORCE_AI_TRAINING=false AIWAF_DISABLE_AI=false AIWAF_AI_ANOMALY_THRESHOLD=0.65 AIWAF_KNOWN_PATHS=/app,/api,/wp-json 8.4 Expected output Updated keyword store and model artifact when thresholds are met. Trainer telemetry via logs and AIWAF::getLastTrainingTelemetry() . 10. Optional GeoIP Enablement AIWAF_GEO_BLOCK_ENABLED=true AIWAF_GEO_BLOCK_COUNTRIES=CN,RU # or allowlist mode AIWAF_GEO_ALLOW_COUNTRIES=US,CA Geo checks run in AIWAF::protect() when enabled. 11. Optional Redis/APCu Setup 10.1 Redis adapter example $redis = new Redis(); $redis->connect('127.0.0.1', 6379); RateLimiter::initAdapter(new RedisAdapter($redis)); 10.2 APCu adapter example RateLimiter::initAdapter(new ApcuAdapter()); 12. Production Baseline Checklist [ ] Package installed and app starts with AIWAF enabled. [ ] php setup.php executed in target environment. [ ] Exempt paths set for health/static/known-safe callbacks. [ ] Rate limits tuned from real traffic patterns. [ ] Header policy tuned to reduce false positives. [ ] Training job scheduled and verified. [ ] Intentional block scenario validated in staging. [ ] Runtime artifact paths persisted across deploys/restarts. 13. Validation Playbook Smoke checks: health/static pass, suspicious probe blocks. Rate-limit checks: burst traffic transitions to 429 and/or IP block. Header checks: low-quality headers trigger expected behavior. Training checks: confirm log readability and artifact/telemetry updates. 14. Troubleshooting Training skipped: verify log path/readability and thresholds. Too many false positives: tune exemptions/known paths and anomaly threshold. Not enough detections: lower anomaly threshold carefully and retrain with representative traffic. Redis/APCu issues: verify extension availability/connectivity and fallback to in-memory temporarily. Resource permissions: ensure read/write on resources/ , rerun php setup.php . 15. Contributor Setup (Repository) composer install composer test php setup.php php cli/detect_and_train.php composer run cover-everything composer run test-adapters-matrix composer run validate-all Suggested docs: README.md .

[ ] Rate limits tuned from real traffic patterns. [ ] Header policy tuned to reduce false positives. [ ] Training job scheduled and verified. [ ] Intentional block scenario validated in staging. [ ] Runtime artifact paths persisted across deploys/restarts. 13. Validation Playbook Smoke checks: health/static pass, suspicious probe blocks. Rate-limit checks: burst traffic transitions to 429 and/or IP block. Header checks: low-quality headers trigger expected behavior. Training checks: confirm log readability and artifact/telemetry updates. 14. Troubleshooting Training skipped: verify log path/readability and thresholds. title: AIWAF Python
text: AIWAF Python How AIWAF works: system architecture Python release candidate 1.1.4 lives in py/aiwaf/ . Install a framework extra for Django, Flask, or FastAPI. The package installs its required aiwaf-rust>=0.2.3 runtime. The package metadata declares Python 3.10 or newer; the selected framework and scientific dependencies may require a newer interpreter. Packages in the monorepo Each package is versioned and released independently. Runtime Package Repository version Primary use Python aiwaf 1.1.8 Django, Flask, and FastAPI protection Node.js aiwaf 1.1.4 Express and Node framework middleware Rust/Python aiwaf-rust 0.2.7 Native Python acceleration and JSON model inference WebAssembly aiwaf-wasm 0.2.4 Rust detection and model primitives for JavaScript Java io.github.aiwaf-project:aiwaf-java 1.3.4 Spring MVC and Jakarta Servlet protection Supported framework integrations include Django, Flask, FastAPI, Express, Fastify, Hapi, Koa, NestJS, Next.js API routes, AdonisJS, Sails.js, Spring MVC, and Jakarta Servlet. Repository layout . ├── py/aiwaf/ Python package and adapters ├── js/ Node.js package and adapters ├── rust/ Rust core and Python bindings │ └── crates/aiwaf_wasm/ WebAssembly bindings ├── java/ Java 17 package ├── tests/ Python integration and parity tests ├── benchmarks/ Python middleware benchmarks ├── examples/ Focused Python examples ├── .github/workflows/ Tests, security checks, and releases ├── README.md Canonical project documentation └── LICENSE Canonical Elastic License 2.0 (see NOTICE) Request controls IP blocklist, exemption, reputation, expiry, and progressive-block handling Sliding-window rate limiting and flood detection Header, method, request-size, content-type, and parameter validation Static and learned malicious keyword detection Honeypot field and form-timing checks UUID probing and tamper detection GeoIP allow/block policies using the bundled MMDB data Route manifests, path-specific overrides, and decorator/annotation exemptions Memory, file, CSV, SQLite, database, and cache-backed runtime state, depending on the runtime Structured request logging and offline training Six-feature anomaly models with Rust, JavaScript, and Java implementations Optional Rust acceleration for Python and optional WebAssembly acceleration for Node.js The runtimes share policy intent and training feature names, but their framework adapters and model implementations remain language-native. Model artifacts are not generally interchangeable across languages. Continue Django setup Flask setup FastAPI setup Architecture and training Framework adapters Operations and migration Rust-owned CSV request pipeline Release candidate: this page documents Python 1.1.8 and Rust/Python 0.2.7 in the current source checkout. Source versions do not establish registry availability. Python 1.1.8 requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.7 ; framework dependencies remain extras. Install the explicit native adapter instead of the existing AIWAF middleware chain. Installing the required Rust dependency does not automatically switch existing applications to this pipeline. Legacy adapters remain available for custom stores and hooks; their configuration and fallback behavior are separate. Rust owns the native CSV pipeline configuration, enforcement order, SQL and keyword inspection, geo/blocklist decisions, rate buckets, form timing, UUID scores, anomaly history/inference, keyword learning, and CSV logging. Python supplies framework routes, authentication facts, GeoIP lookup, bounded request buffering, and response construction. Training and management still have Python interfaces. Continue with the request lifecycle , the native profile , migration , and performance and deployment . Shared Python CSV storage List APIs and command help now use blocklist and allowlist . Earlier import/method/command spellings remain compatibility aliases. Existing CSV filenames and Django model identity are retained so upgrades preserve stored blocks and exemptions; use the package storage constants rather than constructing filenames. Python 1.1.4 standardizes Flask, FastAPI, Django CSV mode, and the explicit native pipeline on blacklist.csv , whitelist.csv , keywords.csv , geo_blocked_countries.csv , and path_exemptions.csv . Keyword frequencies and non-policy runtime history are retained in runtime_metadata.csv . Memory, JSON-file, database, and Django ORM modes keep their existing storage behavior. Integration CSV directory configuration Legacy Flask Set app.config['AIWAF_USE_CSV'] = True and app.config['AIWAF_DATA_DIR'] before initializing AIWAF. Legacy Django Set AIWAF_STORAGE_MODE = "csv" and AIWAF_DATA_DIR in project settings. Legacy FastAPI Pass storage={"backend": "csv", "data_dir": "/absolute/path/aiwaf_data"} to AIWAF . Its default backend remains memory. Native adapters Pass the lowercase data_dir in the dedicated native profile. Native adapters do not inherit legacy framework settings. Startup imports legacy runtime CSV data once, preserving block expiry and metadata. Original sources remain intact; backups and completion markers support recovery and prevent removed entries from returning on restart. Existing canonical policy wins conflicts. Stop old workers before upgrading and use the same absolute directory for the application and CLI. See migration paths and recovery . Flask management searches existing project aiwaf_data and .aiwaf/data before user/package directories. Explicit AIWAF_DATA_DIR or --data-dir takes priority. The five policy files use UTF-8 across Python and Rust. Sharing these files does not make memory rate buckets, model history, or optional memory form timing distributed. Flask and FastAPI native honeypot cache Python 1.1.8 with aiwaf-rust 0.2.7 adds opt-in Redis and supplied-cache timing to both native adapters. CSV remains their default. Rust retains timing rules and exemptions; only timestamp I/O uses the cache. import os profile = { "data_dir": "aiwaf_data", "honeypot_backend": "redis", "honeypot_redis_url": os.environ["AIWAF_REDIS_URL"], "honeypot_cache_namespace": "myapp:honeypot:v1", } # Flask: from aiwaf.flask.csv_pipeline import NativeAIWAF NativeAIWAF(app, config=profile) # FastAPI alternative: # from aiwaf.fast.csv_pipeline import NativeAIWAFMiddleware # app.add_middleware(NativeAIWAFMiddleware, config=profile) For Flask-Caching or a compatible custom object, use honeypot_backend="cache" and pass honeypot_cache=cache to the native adapter. It must provide synchronous get(key) and set(key, value, timeout=seconds) , preserve the timestamp/expiry pair, honor TTL and propagate errors. A false write result means failure; silent/no-op backends are unsuitable. Local caches remain worker-local. Use a shared backend and the same namespace across workers; isolate unrelated applications with different namespaces. Records have a 300-second TTL. Missing/evicted timestamps allow the timing check, while cache errors and invalid records return generic HTTP 503. Expired-page POSTs return 409 until a new GET or TTL expiry; old snapshots are not deleted. FastAPI runs cache-backed native checks in its worker thread pool so synchronous cache I/O does not block the event loop. Other policy stores and legacy middleware behavior are unchanged. Django native honeypot cache Python 1.1.8 with aiwaf-rust 0.2.7 defaults Django native honeypot timing to Django's configured cache. Set honeypot_cache_alias in AIWAF_CSV_PIPELINE to select an alias; it defaults to default . Rust calls a small Python cache adapter for timestamp I/O and retains timing decisions, logical expiry and exemptions. Other policy CSVs and rate-limit configuration are unchanged. AIWAF_CSV_PIPELINE = { "data_dir": "aiwaf_data", "honeypot_cache_alias": "default", } # Configure CACHES["default"] with a shared backend for multiple workers. Redis or Memcached can share timestamps across workers. LocMemCache is supported with a startup warning; it remains worker-local. DummyCache is rejected when honeypot protection is enabled. Cache errors, failed writes and invalid records produce generic HTTP 503; known ignored-cache-error modes are rejected. Entries use a 300-second TTL. Expired-page POSTs return 409 until a new GET or TTL expiry. No eager deletion occurs, so an old POST cannot erase a concurrent refresh. A missing or evicted timestamp allows the POST timing check, as before; cache failure is not treated as a miss. Backends do not transfer existing timestamps. Install the matching Rust extension and restart workers together. Explicit honeypot_backend="csv" retains filesystem timing; "memory" uses Rust's per-engine map. Flask, FastAPI and direct native construction keep CSV as the default. See the Django cache documentation . Training replay protection Python 1.1.6 with aiwaf-rust 0.2.5 uses Rust-owned receipts in Flask, FastAPI, and Django. Reusing requests already handled by training cannot extend or recreate a block. Fresh requests must independently satisfy enforcement rules; models and keyword learning can still reuse historical logs. Keep training_evidence.json across expiry, manual unblocking, log rotation, and restarts. It lives in the policy data directory unless AIWAF_TRAINING_STATE_DIR selects another durable directory. Trainers sharing a blocklist must share that directory. Receipts start with this release and cannot reconstruct decisions made by older versions. Missing native support and corrupt state stop training visibly. Block and receipt writes are separate, so a crash between them can require recovery. Flask CLI listing now filters expired entries without rewriting an older snapshot over blocks concurrently added or refreshed by a trainer. The CLI displays the canonical added_date , with the older timestamp as a fallback. This listing fix and training replay protection address different causes of block changes. A first temporary block defaults to 900 seconds; later reputation decisions can increase its duration. Check the stored expiry rather than assuming every block lasts 24 hours.
