title: PyO3 And WASM Function Reference
text: Bindings API PyO3 And WASM Function Reference How AIWAF works: system architecture 5. PyO3 (Python) Binding Functions Header Validation validate_headers(headers: dict) -> Optional[str] validate_headers_with_config(headers: dict, required_headers: Optional[list[str]], min_score: Optional[int]) -> Optional[str] Matchers and record conversion KeywordMatcher(keywords).first_match(path) returns the first matching keyword or None . RouteMatcher(prefixes).match_index(path) returns the matching prefix index or None . Record helpers include build_records , extract_raw_features , and extract_training_features . Feature Extraction extract_features(records: list[dict], static_keywords: list[str]) -> list[dict] extract_features_batch_with_state(records: list[dict], static_keywords: list[str], state: Optional[dict]) -> dict finalize_feature_state(static_keywords: list[str], state: Optional[dict]) -> dict Recent Behavior Analysis analyze_recent_behavior(entries: list[dict], static_keywords: list[str]) -> Optional[dict] IsolationForest (PyO3) Constructor supports n_estimators , max_samples , contamination , max_features , bootstrap , n_jobs (ignored), random_state , verbose , warm_start . Methods: fit , retrain , anomaly_score , is_anomaly , score_samples , decision_function , predict , to_json , from_json . 6. Isolation Forest Internals And Semantics Core implementation in rust/crates/aiwaf_core/src/lib.rs . fit resets trees unless warm-start append is enabled. retrain temporarily forces warm-start append behavior. anomaly_score : higher means more anomalous. score_samples : higher means more normal (sklearn-aligned direction). decision_function = score_samples - offset_ . predict returns 1 (inlier) and -1 (outlier). Contamination "auto" keeps offset_ = -0.5 ; fixed contamination computes percentile-based offset. 7. WASM Binding Functions validate_headers , validate_headers_with_config extract_features , extract_features_batch_with_state , finalize_feature_state analyze_recent_behavior WASM also exports KeywordMatcher , RouteMatcher , validate_url , validate_content , and record-conversion helpers. WASM IsolationForest class new(config?) , fit , retrain , anomaly_score , is_anomaly , score_samples , decision_function , predict , to_json , from_json Header Handling Notes WASM accepts JS object or Headers . Auto-fills user-agent from navigator.userAgent when absent. Core still expects normalized HTTP_* style names internally. 8. Integration Patterns Python service pattern Build normalized request dict. Run header validation early; block on non- None reason. Build feature records and update state incrementally. Score with IsolationForest and combine with rule outcomes. JS/browser WASM pattern await init() at startup. Use wasm exports in request/event pipeline. Persist forest/state with to_json() as needed. Python ↔ WASM portability Both bindings expose JSON state from the shared Rust core. Validate the serialized feature schema and forest version before exchanging artifacts. Java supports Python Rust-model JSON state; JavaScript-native and legacy artifacts are not generally interchangeable. PyO3 CSV and retained training capabilities The 0.2.2 Python extension additionally exposes CSV snapshot reads/indexed lookups, locked mutations, synchronous append/close operations, shared request policies, route-plan selection, and exemption matching. These are Python binding capabilities; the current WASM API does not expose filesystem CSV transactions or the retained training classes. TrainingCSVReader reads plain/gzip CSV in bounded batches via next_batch(size) , preserving quoted newlines and timing units. NativeTrainingBatch retains features; feature_columns() supplies the six-column order, fit_predict(model) builds/fits/scores in Rust and returns per-IP anomaly statistics, and to_dicts() supports compatibility inspection. NativeTrainingBuilder.add_batch(...) retains incremental feature state; finish() returns a native batch. extract_native_training_features prepares a native feature batch from normalized records and route eligibility. training_date_parts parses supported Apache/ISO parts; Python preserves datetime/epoch semantics and unsupported forms. Native ISO use is opt-in. csv_log_append locks/flushes a row; csv_log_close(path=None) releases cached handles. Policy mutations remain separate transactions. Use the framework adapters and core/training_pipeline.py for normal application integration. Low-level bindings expect the established schemas, units, and argument order; check capabilities before using them with older extensions. Native pipeline API Release candidate: this page documents Python 1.1.8 and Rust/Python 0.2.7 in the current source checkout. Source versions do not establish registry availability. Python 1.1.8 requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.7 ; framework dependencies remain extras. NativeCSVPipeline(profile_json) validates configuration and CSV schemas at construction. begin(...) accepts normalized request facts and returns an engine-owned NativePipelineRequest . finish(context, status, now, content_length, monotonic) finalizes response observations and logging once. Use the framework adapters to construct transport facts and enable monotonic timing. set_model(model) snapshots a trained six-feature Rust IsolationForest; set_model(None) disables inference. seed_history(...) supplies warm history and route-eligibility facts; diagnostics() exposes activation/state counters. The Python binding is separate from WASM exports. Continue with the request lifecycle , the native profile , migration , and performance and deployment . Node/WASM native API Native mode: Node source candidate aiwaf 1.1.4 declares aiwaf-wasm ^0.2.4 . Explicit native registration validates NativeRequestPipeline at startup; missing or incompatible support is an error. There is no JavaScript policy fallback for this engine. Installing the dependency does not switch an existing legacy middleware chain. NativeRequestPipeline(profile_json) validates configuration once. begin(request_json) returns an engine-owned token/decision; finish(context,status,elapsed_ms,now) emits log/policy CSV rows and updates response state once. Hapi uses inspect_body for its deferred parsed-body phase. The engine snapshots a fitted forest with set_model, supports clear_model, and exposes activation/inference/state counters through diagnostics. Node owns filesystem access; the Python NativeCSVPipeline filesystem API is separate. Read the native lifecycle , configuration , deployment and measurements , and migration .

title: Rust Build and Packaging
text: Rust Build and Packaging How AIWAF works: system architecture Native Python build Run these commands in a virtual environment from the monorepo root. Stage the canonical README and LICENSE before changing directory: cp README.md rust/README.md cp LICENSE rust/LICENSE cp NOTICE rust/NOTICE cp -R licenses rust/ python -m pip install maturin cd rust maturin develop cd .. pytest -q rust/tests/test_python_api.py PowerShell users can stage the assets with Copy-Item README.md rust/README.md , Copy-Item LICENSE rust/LICENSE , Copy-Item NOTICE rust/NOTICE , and Copy-Item -Recurse licenses rust/ . These generated package-local assets are ignored by Git. Rust core and WASM cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked -p aiwaf_core cd rust/crates/aiwaf_wasm wasm-pack test --node wasm-pack build --release --target bundler cd ../.. python scripts/patch_wasm_pkg.py cp ../LICENSE crates/aiwaf_wasm/pkg/LICENSE cp ../NOTICE crates/aiwaf_wasm/pkg/NOTICE cp -R ../licenses crates/aiwaf_wasm/pkg/ The metadata script also stages LICENSE, NOTICE, and licenses/. The explicit copy commands above produce the same assets. PowerShell can use Copy-Item for files and Copy-Item -Recurse for directories. Browser applications require a bundler that understands WebAssembly assets; initialize the WASM module before calling its exports. Release manifests The Rust/Python source candidate is 0.2.3; WASM remains 0.2.2. They use independent releases under ELv2. Source versions do not establish registry availability. PyPI: rust/pyproject.toml and rust/Cargo.toml , rust-v0.2.3 , rust-publish.yml . npm: rust/crates/aiwaf_wasm/Cargo.toml , wasm-v0.2.2 , wasm-publish.yml . PyO3 uses ABI3 wheels for Python 3.8 and newer, exporting aiwaf_rust . Verification Confirm import aiwaf_rust works in the interpreter used by the application. Validate model round trips through fit , to_json , from_json , and predict . Python selects available Rust capabilities automatically and falls back when unavailable. WASM performance depends on batch size and conversion cost. CSV validation and performance # From the monorepo root, with the matching installed extension: python scripts/check_native_csv_runtime.py python scripts/check_csv_release_concurrency.py python scripts/benchmark_native_training_boundary.py python scripts/benchmark_native_csv_training.py python scripts/benchmark_native_csv_workloads.py python scripts/benchmark_csv_request_reuse.py python scripts/profile_csv_logging.py The preflight checks module locations, enabled flags, required capabilities, and temporary-file round trips without touching application data. Native snapshot caching and cached log handles are bounded. Closing writers matters before Windows log-directory deletion. Three alternating runs on 10,000 synthetic records measured Apache timestamp speedups of 4.57x on Windows and 3.65x on WSL. Retained features plus a 20-tree Rust fit/predict boundary measured 1.55x and 1.35x. Native ISO parsing was slower on both, so it remains optional. An offline Windows Flask IP/keyword + CSV logging workload measured 5.95 ms native versus 9.18 ms Python. These are scoped measurements, not deployed throughput or complete training speedups. Release validation includes quoting/gzip, timestamp fallback, seeded model parity, chunk equivalence, concurrent mutations, no-op writes, rotation/truncation, and writer reopening. The Linux four-process smoke check retained 160 log rows and 80 blocklist entries. Production load and the full platform/framework matrix still require deployment-specific checks. Publish the Rust dependency before Python releases requiring it. Python release CI can build the matching extension locally for tests; its publication job checks that a compatible dependency is available on PyPI. Local test wheels stay separate from Python release artifacts. Native pipeline release and validation Release candidate: this page documents Python 1.1.8 and Rust/Python 0.2.7 in the current source checkout. Source versions do not establish registry availability. Python 1.1.8 requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.7 ; framework dependencies remain extras. Build/test NativeCSVPipeline and NativePipelineRequest in the installed wheel, not just the source extension. Run rust/tests/test_python_api.py and rust/tests/test_csv_pipeline_api.py . Publish the native wheels before the Python package that requires them. Full benchmark method, measurements and deployment tradeoffs .

title: AIWAF sandbox
text: Testing and security evaluation AIWAF sandbox Run the same request checks across JavaScript, Python, and Java. Compare protected traffic with OWASP Juice Shop, exercise shared Redis state, and test application outcomes with a separate reference fixture. Find the right guide Your goal Guide What it covers Start from scratch First sandbox run Clone, build, verify source versions, and test one endpoint. Look up an integration Runtime and Redis reference Services, ports, databases, state ownership, failure policies, and dependencies. Evaluate protection Validation and reports Smoke, SQL outcomes, payload matrix, TLS, outages, scans, and report interpretation. Understand the security scope OWASP Top 10 coverage Implemented scenarios, assessment boundaries, and remaining gaps. Maintain the stack Operations and troubleshooting Source updates, Redis persistence, profiles, diagnosis, and cleanup. How it works Runner Sends normal requests, simulated clients, and payloads. AIWAF proxy Applies runtime controls before forwarding. Redis Shares supported state under isolated namespaces. Application Juice Shop supplies a vulnerable baseline; the reference fixture supplies outcome assertions. The sandbox repository owns Compose, proxies, fixtures, and runners. BuildKit fetches AIWAF commit 843a35f4fd48b4ef565e3c1ec8a42db9b1c41946 . No adjacent local AIWAF checkout is needed. Use a sandbox revision containing these source-context changes. That commit builds Python/JavaScript 1.1.1 and Java 1.3.2 . Source versions do not establish registry publication. PHP remains a separate Composer integration, excluded from the current fifteen-runtime validation. Evaluate your build Generate reports for the source commit, container images, and configuration you are testing. Run the validation workflow to check source versions, normal traffic, SQL login outcomes, TLS, failures, and dependencies. Passing implemented scenarios does not close an entire OWASP category. See coverage and assessment boundaries before making a security claim. Start your first sandbox run →

title: Operations and troubleshooting
text: How-to guide Operations and troubleshooting Update the GitHub source pin Choose a full commit SHA from the AIWAF repository and review its SDK changes. Change the x-aiwaf-source Git URL fragment in docker-compose.yml , and the matching io.github.aiwaf.source label in all fifteen runtime Dockerfiles. The assessment proxy shares Express's Dockerfile. If SDK versions changed, update aiwaf.version in the Java/Spring example POMs, source-runner version assertions, and affected JS lockfile metadata or Python dependency locks. Rebuild and recreate the selected services, then run run-source-packages.py --verify-only . Run fresh validation and image scans. Keep older reports identified by source, image and time. A branch name may move; the current full SHA makes source selection reproducible. Source labels are build declarations checked against Compose, not cryptographically signed provenance. run-published-packages.py expects registry versions and is not the source-build runner. Refresh dependencies deliberately python examples/sandbox/lock-python-dependencies.py python examples/sandbox/lock-python-dependencies.py --refresh-build-tools The first command refreshes resolved wheel pins/hashes; the second changes only setuptools/wheel while preserving other pins. Review lock diffs, platform requirements and advisories before rebuilding. Node builds use npm ci ; changing manifests requires matching lockfiles. Base digests and Java/Spring security overrides need explicit updates. A pinned source does not prove all package/image inputs produce bit-for-bit identical outputs. Optional profiles Profile Services Purpose assessment security-fixture, aiwaf-assessment Direct/protected outcome checks on loopback 8090/3020. assessment-tls assessment-tls; use with assessment Caddy direct/protected TLS on loopback 8443/8444. trainer aiwaf-trainer Shared access-log training example; independent of the fifteen-runtime validation. tests aiwaf-tests Optional existing test image; not a replacement for source runner/SDK suites. docker compose --profile assessment stop aiwaf-assessment security-fixture docker compose --profile assessment --profile assessment-tls stop assessment-tls The TLS root/private CA material stays in assessment_tls_data . Export only the public root as described in TLS validation . After a large host clock jump, restart Caddy so it can renew its short-lived leaf certificates. Preserve and inspect state docker compose ps docker compose logs --tail 100 aiwaf-django docker compose exec redis redis-cli INFO keyspace docker compose restart aiwaf-django Normal restarts and docker compose down preserve named volumes. down -v deletes stored state and assessment CA data. Do not use it as a routine remedy for false positives. Global Redis flushing destroys other runtimes' evidence; use fresh synthetic clients and inspect service namespaces first. The isolated outage runner is preferable to stopping shared Redis during a test run. Diagnose a failed check Symptom Check Source/version assertion fails Compare resolved Compose source with image labels. Rebuild and recreate; restarting a container does not install a new image. GitHub fetch or registry install fails Check Docker network/proxy access, repository visibility and the full SHA. Do not silently substitute a sibling checkout. Django or burst requests time out Finish scans/builds, verify application/upstream health, and rerun the affected target alone. Record any timeout change; the matrix default is five seconds. Normal requests are blocked after attacks Inspect persistent reputation and actual forwarded client IPs. Verify namespaces and headers; avoid erasing state to hide false positives. TLS verification fails Use localhost, the exported CA and both assessment profiles; inspect certificate time validity and Caddy logs. Keep certificate verification enabled. Grype is slow on Windows Use Docker's Linux engine and the dedicated database volume, not Windows bind-mounted SQLite storage. Inspect scanner errors; scan failure is not a clean result. PHP blocks ordinary routes Use its separate Composer package and autoloader. Sandbox UUID-only path rules are disabled for Juice Shop. PHP remains outside the current validated source scope. Generated files and cleanup Keep source, Dockerfiles, committed locks, fixtures, tests and the latest evidence. Generated reports, bytecode, dependency directories, tool caches and exported TLS certificates are ignored and excluded from images. Delete only exact obsolete paths after confirming they belong to the sandbox; do not remove package manifests, lockfiles or every JSON file. The stack contains a deliberately vulnerable application and synthetic forwarded-IP controls. Use an isolated evaluation environment. The fixture endpoints bind to loopback; normal proxy ports follow Compose bindings. Production network and trust policies need their own review.

title: OWASP Top 10 coverage
text: Topic guide OWASP Top 10 coverage The OWASP Top 10:2025 describes broad application risks. The sandbox combines request observations, confirmed SQL outcomes, reference-application rules, TLS checks and dependency findings. Those are different kinds of evidence. A passing scenario establishes only its tested outcome. It does not close an entire OWASP category. Evaluate each category against your application, deployment, and current dependency findings. Category-by-category scope 2025 category Implemented checks Remaining scope A01 Broken Access Control Reference cross-user reads/writes, anonymous access, role spoofing, protected-field assignment and CSRF. Production identity, ownership, tenant and egress/SSRF policies. AIWAF does not supply application authorization. A02 Security Misconfiguration Sensitive-file/debug exposure and security response headers on direct/protected fixtures. Host/cloud configuration, CORS, cookies and complete deployment audits. A03 Software Supply Chain Failures Manifest/lock fingerprints, Python wheel hashes, pinned images, npm production audits, Grype JS/Python/Java/OS image scans. High advisories remain; PHP, build provenance, signing, exploitability triage and resolved SBOM verification remain separate. A04 Cryptographic Failures Trusted TLS 1.2/1.3; rejection of old protocols, untrusted roots and wrong hostname; PBKDF2 passwords with independent salts. At-rest encryption, production secrets/key management and application-wide cryptography. A05 Injection Two SQL login payloads per integration with token-issuance assertions and benign controls. Other SQL/XSS/XXE/command/LFI-shaped payloads are observations. No blanket injection pass; browser execution, callbacks and additional backend side-effect assertions are needed for other exploit classes. A06 Insecure Design Negative quantity with no side effects, idempotent replay, conflicting payload under the same key and concurrent inventory budget. Application-owned purchase/refund/workflow rules and resource budgets. A07 Authentication Failures Reference session rotation, expiry, logout/revocation; reset actor binding, expiry and single use; MFA requirement, actor binding and replay rejection. Real identity/MFA/reset providers, delivery and production account/session policies. A08 Software or Data Integrity Failures Original signed reference data accepted; modified subject and forged signature rejected. Package signatures, trusted updates, deserialization and other integrity boundaries. A09 Security Logging and Alerting Failures Exactly one correlated redacted failed-login event/alert; modified/truncated history rejected. External SIEM delivery, persistent append-only storage and incident response. A10 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions Generic injected exception plus recovery; isolated live Express Redis and shared upstream failures; Python cache regressions. Every-runtime outages, production failover, rollback and resource cleanup under broader failures. What the reference fixture proves The fixture is separate from Juice Shop. It uses two users, independently salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes with 600,000 iterations, random sessions, test-only reset/MFA controls, isolated inventory and HMAC-protected data. The Compose service starts securely; regression tests also use deliberately broken fixture modes to verify that assertions detect failures. Each check validates response fields and side effects, not merely an HTTP denial. Per-run state is cleaned afterward; fixture signing keys/state are ephemeral. The default control credential is sandbox-assessment-only ; AIWAF_ASSESSMENT_TOKEN overrides it for both Compose and runner. Tokens/passwords are excluded from reports. Reference rules demonstrate an assessment technique, not AIWAF implementations of identity/business policies. Interpret supply-chain findings Run assessment/scan_images.py to scan the fifteen non-PHP images with pinned Grype. Retain image IDs, advisory database metadata, package locations and scan timestamps with your results. A03 image checks fail when high/critical matches exist. Review wont-fix , not-fixed and available fix versions without suppressing findings. Shared packages may produce repeated matches across images; a match count is not a count of distinct exploitable vulnerabilities. A clean npm audit can coexist with OS or other ecosystem findings. Advisory matches require location and exploitability triage. Rebuilt images require matching scan evidence; an older scan does not certify a new image. How to describe a result Identify which scenarios passed, which findings remain, and which controls were not assessed. Avoid “OWASP certified,” “10/10 compliant,” or “all other OWASP categories closed.” Completion of the payload matrix establishes collection of observations without request errors, not universal exploit prevention. See the validation workflow to generate evidence, and application testing to add assertions for your own security boundaries.

title: Runtime and Redis reference
text: Reference Runtime and Redis reference Services and ports Proxy traffic targets juice:3000 inside Docker. The direct host baseline uses port 3001. Test names below work with repeated --target NAME=URL arguments. Test name / framework Compose service Host port Redis DB node / Express aiwaf 3000 0 fastify aiwaf_fastify 3002 1 hapi aiwaf_hapi 3003 2 koa aiwaf_koa 3004 3 nest / NestJS aiwaf_nest 3005 4 next / Next.js aiwaf_next 3006 5 adonis / AdonisJS aiwaf_adonis 3007 6 sails / Sails.js aiwaf_sails 3008 7 django aiwaf-django 3009 8 flask aiwaf-flask 3010 9 fastapi aiwaf-fastapi 3011 10 java / Servlet aiwaf-java 8080 14 spring / Boot aiwaf-spring 8084 14 java-r / JRE with R aiwaf-java-r 8085 14 spring-r / Boot with R aiwaf-spring-r 8086 14 laravel / separate PHP aiwaf-laravel-php81 8081 11 symfony / separate PHP aiwaf-symfony-php82 8082 12 wordpress / separate PHP aiwaf-wordpress-php80 8083 13 Direct fixture security-fixture 8090, loopback Ephemeral application state Protected fixture aiwaf-assessment 3020, loopback 15 TLS direct / protected assessment-tls 8443 / 8444, loopback None PHP is excluded from the current source runner. R variants run the Java engine in an R-containing image; they are not separate R AIWAF packages. State ownership and persistence Redis 7 uses AOF persistence in redis_data , has no published host port, and must pass its health check before protected services start. Services isolate state by database and key prefix. Java integrations share DB 14 with separate sandbox:java: , sandbox:spring: , sandbox:java-r: , and sandbox:spring-r: storage prefixes. JavaScript uses rate-limit lists through the cache adapter. Django uses its native Redis cache for rate limits, honeypot and anomaly history; WATCH/MULTI updates preserve serialized buckets across concurrent writers. Flask/FastAPI use a shared rate-limit cache. Java stores engine state, reputation and distributed counters. PHP uses the Redis extension and RedisAdapter for rate counters. Python/JavaScript model and blocklist storage retains supported adapter backends. A Redis rate cache does not move all state into Redis. Workers of one service must share its namespace for an aggregate budget. Startup clearing is disabled; rate keys expire and restarts preserve state. docker compose exec redis redis-cli INFO keyspace docker compose exec redis redis-cli -n 14 --scan --pattern 'sandbox:*' Cache failure policies Runtime Behavior Settings JavaScript Sanitized rate-cache failures produce generic 503 responses in closed mode. AIWAF_RATE_CACHE_FAILURE_MODE=closed by default; open selects fail-open behavior. Python Typed RateCacheUnavailable errors produce generic 503 responses. Invalid requested Redis configurations no longer silently switch to memory. AIWAF_RATE_CACHE_BACKEND=redis , AIWAF_REDIS_URL , AIWAF_RATE_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX . rediss:// delegates to redis-py; the minimal fallback driver lacks TLS. Java Standalone Redis with bounded waits, default closed policy. AIWAF_REDIS_FAILURE_MODE=fail_closed or fail_open . Connection/socket/pool waits: 1000/2000/250 ms. JavaScript retains compatibility with legacy cache configurations. Closed mode rejects failed operations on the selected cache; it does not establish that every adapter configuration selects Redis. Flask invalid backend setup fails initialization; FastAPI invalid runtime cache configuration is rejected. Shared JavaScript upstream connection failures return generic 502 bad_gateway . See live outage scope . SDK and request-inspection changes The pinned commit contains Python/JavaScript 1.1.1 and Java 1.3.2 source: Python/JavaScript SQL inspection, Java SQL rules and keyword-learning safety, Java decoded query/body previews, JavaScript JSON body handling, Python atomic rate updates, and sanitized Redis failures. Source and registry releases are independent. Rust/WASM dependencies are resolved separately from that source snapshot. Rust/Python 0.2.2 is now published; inspect installed versions rather than assuming the pinned source revision selects the newest accelerator. Node imports aiwaf . Plain Java reads /app/aiwaf.json with environment overrides and supports AIWAF_CONFIG_FILE . Spring uses Boot auto-configuration and route discovery. Its sandbox forwarded-IP trust covers 172.16.0.0/12 ; change AIWAF_SANDBOX_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS to your actual proxy CIDRs elsewhere. Dependency hardening Node: npm ci , compiler build stage, digest-pinned Node 22 slim runtime, npm 12.2.0, patched bundled undici and brace-expansion. Python: refreshed digest-pinned 3.11 base, Linux x86_64/CPython 3.11 wheel hashes, setuptools 84.0.0 and wheel 0.48.0. Java: Jackson 2.22.3; Spring Boot 4.0.8 overrides Jackson 2/3 to 2.22.3/3.1.7 and Tomcat to 11.0.25. Java/R: patched Ubuntu OpenSSL 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.16 packages. Runtime images copy their own application and shared helpers. Tool caches, TLS material, reports and build outputs are excluded from build contexts. These measures reduce known findings; they are not provenance verification or a resolved SBOM. Read remaining advisory findings .

title: Your first sandbox run
text: Tutorial Your first sandbox run You will start Juice Shop, Redis, and fifteen non-PHP proxies, then verify their source versions and test one endpoint. Run every command from the sandbox repository root. 1. Check requirements Docker Desktop using Linux containers, or Docker Engine with BuildKit and Compose additional-context support. Git, Python 3.10+, and network access to GitHub and package registries. Host Node.js only for JavaScript unit tests outside Docker. Time and disk space for Node, Python, Java, and R image builds. docker version docker compose version git --version python --version 2. Clone the sandbox git clone https://github.com/aayushgauba/sandbox.git cd sandbox python -m pip install requests Use a sandbox revision containing run-source-packages.py and the GitHub source contexts. x-aiwaf-source in Compose pins AIWAF commit 843a35f4fd48b4ef565e3c1ec8a42db9b1c41946 . BuildKit clones it automatically. A host SDK installation or adjacent checkout does not select the SDK inside the image. 3. Build the validated integrations docker compose up -d --build aiwaf aiwaf_fastify aiwaf_hapi aiwaf_koa aiwaf_nest aiwaf_next aiwaf_adonis aiwaf_sails aiwaf-django aiwaf-flask aiwaf-fastapi aiwaf-java aiwaf-spring aiwaf-java-r aiwaf-spring-r docker compose ps Compose starts Redis and Juice Shop dependencies. Without a service selection, docker compose up -d --build also starts the default PHP integrations. PHP is outside this validation scope. Checkpoint: Redis and Juice Shop should be healthy and all selected proxies running. The baseline is http://localhost:3001 ; Express protection uses http://localhost:3000 . 4. Verify the installed source python examples/sandbox/run-source-packages.py --verify-only The verifier compares each running proxy's io.github.aiwaf.source label with the resolved Compose context, checks Python/JavaScript 1.1.1 and Java 1.3.2, checks installation paths, and verifies the Java SQL-inspection class. Stale containers fail with a rebuild-required assertion. results_local_versions.json records the installed SDKs under examples/sandbox/ . The filename denotes local Docker execution; github_source identifies remote source and commit. 5. Test a protected endpoint python examples/sandbox/smoke-test.py --target node=http://127.0.0.1:3000 --burst-workers 16 --output examples/sandbox/results_first_smoke.json python examples/sandbox/validate-login-bypass.py --target node=http://127.0.0.1:3000 --output examples/sandbox/results_first_login.json The smoke check requires normal requests to succeed, automation and excess traffic to be denied, and benign invalid credentials to reach Juice Shop as a 401. The SQL check requires two payloads to fail to obtain an authentication token; token values are omitted from reports. Continue with full validation . If a check fails, inspect docker compose logs --tail 100 aiwaf and troubleshooting . ← Overview Validation →

title: Validation and reports
text: How-to guide Validation and reports Run the source validation workflow Start the fifteen integrations from the tutorial , then the optional reference services. Run checks sequentially to avoid build/scan load distorting request timeouts. docker compose --profile assessment up -d --build security-fixture aiwaf-assessment python -m pip install requests python -m unittest discover -s examples/sandbox -p 'test_*.py' node --test examples/sandbox/common/redis-cache.test.js examples/sandbox/common/proxy.test.js python examples/sandbox/run-source-packages.py The runner verifies source labels and versions, then executes smoke, SQL login, payload matrix, post-matrix SQL, reference checks and nine production npm audits: eight proxy trees and the SDK. It excludes PHP. --verify-only performs installed-source checks. --skip-completed accepts prior suite reports only when the recorded source URL/commit matches; omit it for a fresh run. Interpret each check Check What success establishes Limit Smoke Normal/lowercase headers succeed; automation and excess traffic are denied; benign JSON login reaches the app. Not a complete attack evaluation. Burst checks need accepted and denied requests, so blanket blocking fails. SQL login Two SQL payloads cannot issue a token; invalid credentials supply the control. Specific exploit outcomes only. Tokens are omitted. Payload matrix All selected observations complete without request errors. Exit 0 does not mean every payload was denied or every exploit prevented. Reference fixture Status, response fields and state changes enforce each tested application rule. Application-owned controls; an unrelated WAF 403 cannot count as success. npm/image audit Advisory query and matched dependency findings are recorded. Package locations and exploitability still need triage. The legacy attack suite classifies 403/405/409/429 as blocked; these statuses can come from another layer. Default legacy probes can also be rejected by header validation before payload inspection. A block percentage is not a demonstrated detection rate. The newer matrix uses browser headers except in scenarios designed to alter them. Rate-limit and brute-force scenarios retain one public client IP throughout, then generate a fresh IP for the next scenario. Other probes rotate per request. Redis is not flushed, so retained reputation may reveal false positives after attack traffic. Target one runtime or resume observations python examples/sandbox/smoke-test.py --target django=http://127.0.0.1:3009 --burst-workers 16 python examples/sandbox/validate-login-bypass.py --target java=http://127.0.0.1:8080 python examples/sandbox/validate-runtime-matrix.py --exclude laravel --exclude symfony --exclude wordpress --output examples/sandbox/results_local_payload.json The matrix's default per-request timeout is five seconds. --timeout changes that requirement; disclose any change when reporting results. --resume retains saved baselines and targets without errors, and reruns failed targets. Keep resumes within the same source/configuration; the matrix alone does not verify commit provenance. Extended checks with TLS Caddy exposes only loopback ports 8443/8444. Its internal CA stays in a dedicated Docker volume. Export the public root certificate; pass it explicitly to the runner without changing host trust. docker compose --profile assessment --profile assessment-tls up -d --build security-fixture aiwaf-assessment assessment-tls New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force examples/sandbox/assessment/.tls docker compose --profile assessment --profile assessment-tls cp assessment-tls:/data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt examples/sandbox/assessment/.tls/root.crt python examples/sandbox/assessment/run.py --extended --fixture https://localhost:8443 --fixture https://localhost:8444 --ca-file examples/sandbox/assessment/.tls/root.crt --tls-url https://localhost:8443 --tls-url https://localhost:8444 --npm-audit --local-runtime-scope --output examples/sandbox/results_local_owasp_extended.json Tests require trusted TLS 1.2/1.3, rejection of old protocols, untrusted roots and incorrect hostnames. Client-side inability to test an old protocol is not_assessed , not a server pass. Both profiles are needed because TLS depends on the fixture/proxy. Caddy preserves synthetic client IPs for loopback assessment; that trust arrangement is not a production proxy policy. For HTTP-only checks, use both --fixture http://localhost:8090 and --fixture http://localhost:3020 with --extended --allow-local-http . HTTP transport remains unassessed. Omitting --npm-audit leaves the advisory query unassessed. Isolated failures and dependency scans python examples/sandbox/assessment/outages.py python examples/sandbox/audit-published-proxies.py --include-sdk --output examples/sandbox/results_local_npm_audits.json python examples/sandbox/assessment/scan_images.py python examples/sandbox/assessment/render_report.py Outage tests run an isolated Express process with actual Redis/upstream connection refusals. They require generic 503 with no application call for Redis, and generic 502 for upstream failure. They do not stop shared Redis or demonstrate failover in all runtimes. Python outage behavior has separate SDK unit/HTTP regressions. Grype 0.120.0 is pinned by image digest, scans fifteen built images including OS packages, mounts the Docker socket and uses sandbox_grype_db for its advisory database. It exits 1 on high/critical findings or scan errors; lower findings are retained. --service selects images; --resume reuses raw reports only when filesystem layers and runtime configuration match, retaining original scan dates. Report reference Files under examples/sandbox/ Contents results_local_versions.json , results_local_run.json , results_local_validation.md Source runner provenance, suite exits, aggregate validation. Existing reports may describe an earlier run; inspect timestamps/source. results_local_smoke.json , results_local_login*.json , results_local_payload.json Runtime requests, SQL outcomes, matrix observations. results_local_owasp*.json , results_local_outages.json , results_local_npm_audits.json Reference/TLS outcomes, isolated failures and npm audits. results_local_image_advisories.json , results_owasp_scan_*.json Image finding summaries and raw package-location evidence. results_local_owasp_summary.md Category totals, failed image checks, remaining scope and grouped high/critical findings. The report renderer reads the results_local_* files together; it does not reconcile timestamps or source provenance for every component. Generate fresh components before treating an aggregate as current. Reports are ignored by Git and excluded from build images. Assessment statuses are pass , fail , error , and not_assessed . Failures/errors cause exit 1. A clean npm audit can coexist with OS image advisories. OWASP scope explains the remaining work.

title: Testing an AIWAF-protected application
text: Testing an AIWAF-protected application Test both the application's successful responses and the protection decisions that can stop a request before its handler. Start with deterministic limits, then add the full middleware stack and deployment checks. Choose the right test boundary Layer What to verify What it proves Application tests Validation, authentication, business rules, and successful response bodies. The handler behaves correctly when reached. Focused protection tests An allowed request, a rejected request, and a scoped exemption for one enabled check. The middleware is registered and enforces the intended policy. Full application integration Actual middleware order, route manifest, headers, storage, and known model fixtures. The checks work together with your framework and application. Deployment tests Real proxy/client identity, repeated requests across workers, shared state, and health probes. The deployed topology behaves as intended. Keep a successful request beside each rejection assertion. A suite where every request fails can hide a broken registration, missing route, or overly broad policy. The examples below enable only rate limiting so an unrelated header or model check cannot cause an accidental pass. Isolate state before writing assertions Use a fresh application or test client lifecycle and dedicated data, log, and model locations. CSV files and Redis state do not roll back with a database transaction. Give parallel workers separate cache namespaces, databases, or directories. Keep one namespace shared only for tests explicitly checking cross-worker behavior. Use fixed route budgets and an isolated manifest path. A discovered route policy can override the global limit, so test the effective route policy. Keep the client identity stable while testing a bucket. Use a new identity when testing independent clients. Use a known JSON model fixture for anomaly decisions. Do not train on live traffic as part of a deterministic application test. For window expiry tests, control the clock at the component boundary or use a dedicated timed integration test. Avoid long sleeps in ordinary tests. Django's test runner creates test databases, but caches are not automatically isolated or cleared between tests. Use a dedicated test cache before clearing it. See Django's testing overview . Write and run Flask protection tests Create an empty working directory, install aiwaf[flask] , and save this complete file as test_flask_protection.py . It builds a new application and temporary CSV directory for every test, explicitly selects memory counters, and pins both route budgets. python -m pip install "aiwaf[flask]" test_flask_protection.py """Run with: python -m unittest discover -s examples/testing -p test_flask_protection.py -v""" from pathlib import Path import tempfile import unittest from flask import Flask from aiwaf.flask import AIWAF, aiwaf_exempt, aiwaf_exempt_from class ProtectionTests(unittest.TestCase): def setUp(self): # A new application and state directory for every test. directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".ci-protection-validation-", dir=Path.cwd()) self.addCleanup(directory.cleanup) app = Flask(__name__) app.config.update( TESTING=True, AIWAF_USE_CSV=True, AIWAF_DATA_DIR=directory.name, AIWAF_RATE_CACHE_BACKEND="memory", AIWAF_PATH_MANIFEST=str(Path(directory.name) / "paths.json"), AIWAF_RATE_WINDOW=60, AIWAF_RATE_MAX=3, AIWAF_RATE_FLOOD=100, AIWAF_PATH_RULES=[ {"PREFIX": path, "RATE_LIMIT": {"WINDOW": 60, "MAX": 3, "FLOOD": 100}} for path in ("/api/message", "/api/preview") ], ) @app.get("/api/message") def message(): return {"message": "Protected"} @app.get("/health") @aiwaf_exempt def health(): return {"ok": True} @app.get("/api/preview") @aiwaf_exempt_from("rate_limit") def preview(): return {"message": "Preview"} AIWAF(app, middlewares=["rate_limit"]) self.client = app.test_client() def test_protected_route_throttles(self): for _ in range(3): response = self.client.get("/api/message") self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200) self.assertEqual(response.json, {"message": "Protected"}) response = self.client.get("/api/message") self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 429) self.assertEqual(response.json, {"error": "too_many_requests"}) def test_health_stays_available_after_throttling(self): for _ in range(4): self.client.get("/api/message") response = self.client.get("/health") self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200) self.assertEqual(response.json, {"ok": True}) def test_selective_exemption_bypasses_rate_limit(self): self.assertEqual( [self.client.get("/api/preview").status_code for _ in range(5)], [200] * 5, ) if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main() python -m unittest discover -s . -p test_flask_protection.py -v Expect three passing tests. The first verifies three successful responses followed by HTTP 429 and the exact too_many_requests JSON body. The others verify health availability after the protected route is throttled and that a selective rate-limit exemption permits repeated requests. Checkpoint: Change the expected throttle status from 429 to 200 and rerun: that assertion should fail. Restore it afterward. This confirms the test can detect the behavior it claims to check. This fixture exercises AIWAF behavior independently. In your own project, also test your actual app factory and live routes so a mistake in production registration cannot be hidden by a separate fixture. Write and run Django protection tests In a separate empty directory, install aiwaf[django] and save both files below. The fixture uses Django's test client, ORM-backed AIWAF stores, an in-memory SQLite test database, and a dedicated local-memory cache. The URL configuration is the test module itself. python -m pip install "aiwaf[django]" django_test_settings.py """Settings for this standalone example, separate from your application's settings.""" from pathlib import Path SECRET_KEY = "local-documentation-test-key" INSTALLED_APPS = ["aiwaf.django"] DATABASES = {"default": {"ENGINE": "django.db.backends.sqlite3", "NAME": ":memory:"}} DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD = "django.db.models.BigAutoField" # Only for this standalone fixture: create AIWAF tables without generated migrations. MIGRATION_MODULES = {"aiwaf": None} ROOT_URLCONF = "test_django_protection" ALLOWED_HOSTS = ["testserver"] MIDDLEWARE = ["aiwaf.django.middleware.RateLimitMiddleware"] CACHES = { "default": { "BACKEND": "django.core.cache.backends.locmem.LocMemCache", "LOCATION": "documentation-protection-tests", } } AIWAF_USE_CSV = False AIWAF_PATH_MANIFEST = str(Path(__file__).with_name("unused-test-manifest.json")) AIWAF_RATE_WINDOW = 60 AIWAF_RATE_MAX = 3 AIWAF_RATE_FLOOD = 100 AIWAF_EXEMPT_PATHS = ["/health"] AIWAF_SETTINGS = { "PATH_RULES": [ {"PREFIX": "/api/message", "RATE_LIMIT": {"WINDOW": 60, "MAX": 3, "FLOOD": 100}}, {"PREFIX": "/api/preview", "DISABLE": ["rate_limit"]}, ] } test_django_protection.py """Run from this directory using django_test_settings; see /docs/testing.""" from django.core.cache import cache from django.http import JsonResponse from django.test import TestCase from django.urls import path def message(request): return JsonResponse({"message": "Protected"}) def health(request): return JsonResponse({"ok": True}) def preview(request): return JsonResponse({"message": "Preview"}) urlpatterns = [ path("api/message", message), path("health", health), path("api/preview", preview), ] class ProtectionTests(TestCase): def setUp(self): # django_test_settings points only at a dedicated local-memory test cache. cache.clear() self.addCleanup(cache.clear) def test_protected_route_throttles(self): for _ in range(3): response = self.client.get("/api/message") self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200) self.assertEqual(response.json(), {"message": "Protected"}) response = self.client.get("/api/message") self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 429) self.assertEqual(response.json(), {"error": "too_many_requests"}) def test_health_stays_available_after_throttling(self): for _ in range(4): self.client.get("/api/message") response = self.client.get("/health") self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200) self.assertEqual(response.json(), {"ok": True}) def test_selective_exemption_bypasses_rate_limit(self): self.assertEqual( [self.client.get("/api/preview").status_code for _ in range(5)], [200] * 5, ) python -m django test test_django_protection --settings=django_test_settings -v 2 Expect three passing tests and creation/destruction of the test database. TestCase isolates ORM changes; setUp() and cleanup clear only the dedicated local-memory cache. The standalone fixture disables AIWAF migrations to create its tables directly. In an existing project, keep your real migrations, include AIWAF in INSTALLED_APPS , and run your application's tests with its dedicated test settings. Adapt these assertions to the routes from the Django setup guide . Keep another suite using your real ROOT_URLCONF and complete MIDDLEWARE list: this focused fixture intentionally exercises only the rate limiter. Django route-policy detail This fixture uses AIWAF_EXEMPT_PATHS for health and a PATH_RULES entry disabling only rate_limit for preview. In the current source, the rate limiter runs before Django resolves the view, while decorator detection reads request.resolver_match . A selective decorator alone did not bypass the limiter in this full test-client request. Use the explicit path policy for this case, and test decorators through your actual middleware stack. Apply the same assertions to other frameworks The status sequence and test structure above belong to these Python fixtures. For other runtimes, use that runtime's configuration names, response contract, and policy precedence. FastAPI: use its test client against the actual ASGI application. Keep the client in a context manager when startup/shutdown initializes resources. Give each test its own policy/state configuration; see the FastAPI setup guide . Node.js: create a fresh app and AIWAF middleware instance per test. Use the framework's injection facility or an HTTP client against an ephemeral local port. Verify a normal response, configured throttle/block response, and exemption. See Node.js operations . Java: test the engine decision independently, then exercise the registered Spring filter or Servlet filter through your framework test harness. Keep shared Redis integration tests separate from memory-backed tests. See Java operations . Expand to the full protection stack Headers and parsing: pair valid browser/API requests with requests violating your configured requirements. Assert the rejection reason or body as well as status. Exemptions: verify that the intended check is bypassed and that another enabled check still runs. The rate-only examples prove the bypass, but do not prove other checks remain active. Flood and reputation: distinguish a soft throttle from a hard block. Verify persistent state and later requests separately using disposable storage. Models: cover a known normal sample, a known anomaly, and missing/invalid model handling for your configured runtime. Keep training tests separate from inference tests. Route discovery: generate the manifest from the test application's live route table, verify the protected route is present, and repeat the behavior assertions with the manifest loaded. Observation: check the expected log record and response status, including denied requests, without relying on a production log file. For Redis or multiple workers, send a combined request sequence across workers using the same client identity and bucket. Assert the aggregate budget, expiry behavior, and configured backend-failure behavior. A single-process in-memory test cannot establish those guarantees. Run the examples in continuous integration From the AIWAF website checkout, the checked-in examples run with these commands. Install the relevant framework extras first. python -m unittest discover -s examples/testing -p test_flask_protection.py -v cd examples/testing python -m django test test_django_protection --settings=django_test_settings -v 2 Run application and focused protection tests on each change. Run shared-backend and deployed-topology checks in a separate integration job with disposable services. Save failure output and effective policy configuration so failures can be reproduced locally. Diagnose a failing protection test Failure Check next Expected 429, got 200 Middleware registration, route/IP exemptions, effective manifest rules, changing client identity, and counters split across workers. First request already rejected Leaked cache/blocklist state, missing required headers, route mismatch, or another enabled check. Passes alone, fails in the suite Shared storage/cache keys, module-level app reuse, test order, and model/manifest files left by another test. Expected JSON, got HTML or a redirect Wrong URL, trailing-slash routing, framework exception handling, or a response produced by the application/proxy. Use the Redis-enabled multi-runtime sandbox for pinned GitHub source builds and cross-runtime checks. Follow the first-run tutorial , run SQL, TLS, outage and dependency checks , and review OWASP coverage and limits before interpreting results. Continue with troubleshooting , configuration reference , and state ownership across workers . Legacy native CSV and training regression checks python aiwaf_test.py --python-only --coverage python manage.py test tests.django python scripts/check_native_csv_runtime.py python scripts/check_csv_release_concurrency.py Django regression tests belong in tests/django as Django test cases discovered by manage.py test . Core and Flask/FastAPI tests use their corresponding pytest suites. The release runner also checks canonical source-to-test layout, line/branch coverage, and newly uncovered callables. Passing a coverage percentage alone does not satisfy the callable baseline gate. Test native/fallback parity with explicit adapter settings or native_override(False) : an environment-only toggle can be overridden by already configured Django settings in a combined suite. Exercise invalid/quoted/gzip logs, duplicate keyword updates, expiry, cross-worker changes, model parity, and close/reopen after rotation. Use isolated temporary files and close writer handles before cleanup. Native pipeline validation Test each framework adapter with normal routes and SQL/PHP probes, bounded JSON/form inspection, decorator precedence, unknown routes, model activation, clock adjustments, opaque context ownership, single finalization and log output. Test CSV timing across engines/workers and memory isolation/restart behavior separately. Streaming ASGI logs finalize at response start. Release validation includes tests/core/test_csv_pipeline.py , framework test_csv_pipeline.py suites and installed-wheel rust/tests/test_csv_pipeline_api.py . Compare full protected requests with a matched framework-only baseline . Native Node regression checks Native tests exercise real WASM (no mock fallback), parsed SQL/JSON escapes and limits, safe Unicode, header caps, timing/isolation, flood expiry, persisted blocks/learned keywords, write errors, model activation, streaming and engine-owned finalization. Transport tests cover Express, Fastify, Hapi, Koa, Nest, Next and Adonis; unknown paths must be tested alongside registered handlers. Read the native lifecycle , configuration , deployment and measurements , and migration . Verify the current Python and Node source The source targets are Python 1.1.4 with Rust/Python 0.2.3 and Node 1.1.2 with WASM 0.2.2. Run the framework-specific suites with the same dependencies and configuration as the deployed application. # From the AIWAF monorepo root, with test dependencies installed. python -m pytest tests/core tests/flask tests/fast tests/test_cli.py tests/test_cli_init_detection.py python manage.py test tests.django # Reproduce the committed Node dependency tree. npm ci --prefix js npm audit --prefix js # Build the CommonJS native fixture used by Jest. wasm-pack build rust/crates/aiwaf_wasm --release --target nodejs --out-dir pkg-node-test export AIWAF_NATIVE_TEST_MODULE="$PWD/rust/crates/aiwaf_wasm/pkg-node-test/aiwaf_wasm.js" npm run test:coverage --prefix js npm run test:wasm --prefix js npm run test:native --prefix js In PowerShell, replace export with: $env:AIWAF_NATIVE_TEST_MODULE = (Resolve-Path 'rust/crates/aiwaf_wasm/pkg-node-test/aiwaf_wasm.js').Path The Node release workflow builds this fixture for Jest and checks the actual installed WASM engine separately. Framework test dependencies include patched Fastify 5 and NestJS 11; Jest 30 uses a cookie-module transform for Node 22 compatibility. Audit development dependencies as well as production dependencies. For Python CSV upgrades, verify temporary and permanent blocks, expiry metadata, keywords and counts, IP/pattern exemptions, country lists, path exemptions, and UTF-8 data. Restart after removing a migrated block to verify that the old source is not replayed. Test malformed input and interrupted migration using an isolated directory. See migration semantics . For native Node mode, verify initialization failure, bounded parsed bodies, unknown-route checks, actual model inference counters, finish/close finalization, persistence on reconstruction, and worker isolation. Native Node files and legacy CLI stores have different schemas. See the current validation results . October 2026 release upgrade The prepared source versions are Python 1.1.6 , Rust/Python 0.2.5 , Node.js 1.1.4 , WASM 0.2.4 , and Java 1.3.4 . These are source targets; verify registry availability before installing. Python requires aiwaf-rust>=0.2.5 , including the TrainingEvidence API. Node offline training requires the matching WASM receipt API. Back up policies, logs, models, and training evidence. Use the same absolute data and evidence directories for application workers and CLI trainers. Install the matching native companion before upgrading its host package: Rust before Python, WASM before Node. Preserve training_evidence.json and node_training_evidence.json across expiry, unblocking, restarts, and log rotation. Stop older file writers and restart all workers on the new code. Mixing old unlocked writers with new writers can still lose updates. In staging, train twice on identical logs, then verify handled evidence does not recreate a removed or expired block. Add genuinely fresh requests and confirm they must independently satisfy the enforcement threshold. Verify that listing and expiry checks preserve concurrently refreshed blocks and unrelated IPs. Check the raw expiry and backend location if entries disappear unexpectedly. Java CSV and file storage Java 1.3.4 reloads current storage under a shared JVM and OS sidecar lock for each operation. Reads filter expiry without rewriting disk; mutations preserve other instances' updates and report persistence failures. This adds file I/O. Java model training still does not add blocklist entries. Rate buckets and other per-engine memory state retain their existing isolation. Lock recovery Python training uses an OS file lock; Java CSV/file OS locks also release on process exit. Keep their stable sidecar lock files in place while workers run. Node uses lock directories for training and legacy CSV mutations; a crash can leave them behind. Confirm the owning process has stopped before removing a Node lock directory. Do not delete training receipts to clear a lock: doing so loses handled-evidence history. Release checks Local validation passed 247 Node tests across 67 suites with the coverage gate, 215 Java tests with 3 skips, and 38 Rust/WASM native tests. After the native dependency bump, 11 affected Python packaging tests passed through the appropriate Django and pytest runners. These checks do not replace full release CI, dependency audits, signing, or operating-system wheel builds. Build Linux/macOS Rust wheels using the release matrix; the local bundle contains a Windows x86-64 wheel. For release maintainers: publish the WASM companion, refresh the Node lockfile from the registry to record its actual integrity, then run npm ci and the native integration checks. Do not substitute an older native dependency to satisfy a stale packaging test. See the changelog .

title: Troubleshooting and Verification
text: Troubleshooting and Verification CLI rejects --app app.py --app takes a Python import target, not a filename. For app.py containing app = Flask(__name__) , run from its directory: aiwaf init --framework flask --app app:app For a factory use app:create_app . For Django use --framework django --settings project.settings . Install dependencies and load the application's configuration in the same environment; discovery imports the live application. Manifest has only / and static routes Confirm the imported file is your intended application, all blueprints/routers are registered, and the app factory finishes before discovery: python -c "import app; print(app.__file__); print(*sorted(r.rule for r in app.app.url_map.iter_rules()), sep='\n')" This diagnostic is for a Flask module-level app. Regenerate the manifest after registering additional routes. An unimported blueprint cannot appear in the live route table. Website setup page returns 404 or 500 /docs/python/setup redirects to /docs/python/setup/django . /python/setup/django redirects to the same canonical guide. Both app runners register the shared documentation blueprint. Unknown pages return 404; errors inside an existing template remain server errors. Check which checkout the WSGI worker imports and which entrypoint the host uses. Deploy documentation.py and all templates together, including shared includes. Reload the host's web application or restart workers after updating source/dependencies. Read the server traceback for import errors, missing includes, or initialization failures. A 500 page alone does not identify the cause. python -m unittest discover -s tests -v python -c "from wsgi import application; print(application.url_map)" curl -i https://aiwaf.org/health The import check initializes the actual website and may create runtime files. Tests isolate documentation routing and rendering; a passing test does not establish that the deployed worker has reloaded. /health is liveness, not database/cache readiness. Normal traffic is blocked, or test traffic is never blocked Compare response details and logs with the selected middleware, route plan, client IP, headers, and block/reputation state. A 403 may come from AIWAF or a proxy; avoid attributing it without evidence. Rate throttling can have different status semantics from a deterministic block. Private clients, health paths, static paths, or route annotations may be exempt. Local curl success alone does not demonstrate protection for public clients. To exercise header validation, use a non-exempt route and a client context matching deployment; include representative User-Agent/Accept headers and browser-standard headers such as Accept-Language/Accept-Encoding in the normal case. Plain curl requests can be rejected by the website's header policy; use a browser or matching headers to check protected documentation. The website explicitly exempts /health for liveness probes. Configure a small staging threshold and test below, at, and above the boundary. Do not disable protection globally to resolve a single route. Client IP or multi-worker counters look wrong Inspect address extraction for your adapter and the actual forwarding-header chain. Have the trusted outer proxy overwrite client-supplied headers. Java has explicit trusted proxy CIDRs; Python/Node resolution follows their own rules. File persistence is separate from a shared rate cache. Redis configuration must resolve to an active shared backend. Flask rejects invalid Redis configuration at initialization; runtime Redis rate-cache failures return HTTP 503; test enforcement across two workers and examine initialization logs. Use the same rate-key prefix for workers sharing one service, and distinct prefixes for unrelated services. Training produces no usable model Verify that the trainer reads the actual log path/format, logs include response observations, minimum sample thresholds are met, and the output model is written where runtime inference loads it. Representative normal traffic is needed; forced training does not repair missing or malformed inputs. Inspect trainer/model help for the installed adapter: aiwaf flask train --help aiwaf flask model --help # Django uses its management commands: python manage.py detect_and_train --help Python requires JSON model state. Regenerate legacy executable artifacts rather than renaming their extension. Verify model load diagnostics after deployment/reload. Models with different feature schemas or native formats need a supported conversion path or retraining. Verification before publishing documentation Render every page; check internal links, fragment anchors, setup redirects, and unknown-page behavior. Then test code samples with the installed runtime in a clean staging environment, including a normal request and an intentional rejection. Finally test the public URLs after deployment. These are separate checks. See configuration , migration , and the runtime operations pages for the exact settings and supported tools. Rust and CSV diagnostics The explicit native pipeline fails startup if native API/schema/profile validation fails. Check for NativeCSVPipeline support in the deployed interpreter. Installing Rust does not switch a legacy chain to the new adapter. Unknown keys and legacy uppercase settings are invalid in the native profile; Rust-disable compatibility flags do not supply a fallback. python -c "import sys, aiwaf_rust; print(sys.executable); print(aiwaf_rust.__file__)" python scripts/check_native_csv_runtime.py For retained legacy integrations, if installation succeeds but behavior stays on Python, check the application's interpreter, worker restart, extension capabilities, and AIWAF_USE_RUST / AIWAF_RUST_CSV . Framework settings take precedence over the standalone environment flag. Unicode/custom parser paths may deliberately use Python; ISO parsing does so by default because it measured faster. A PHP probe returning 404 may be reaching an unprotected application. Verify the deployed WSGI import is the protected app (the website uses from app import app as application ), inspect registered request hooks, and check route/IP exemptions. A path missing from the route table is not automatically blocked: keyword, rate, and anomaly policies decide whether to deny it. For Windows log-directory deletion failures, stop requests and close cached CSV log writers first. For HTTP 503 from rate limiting, check Redis availability or required native CSV capabilities. A freshly trained FastAPI model needs an explicit reload or application restart. Existing CSV data is missing from the CLI First compare the application's data directory with the directory printed by the CLI. A command launched from another working directory may select a different store. Pin the same absolute AIWAF_DATA_DIR , or use aiwaf flask --data-dir /absolute/path/aiwaf_data status . Python 1.1.4 fixes project and user-directory discovery and imports the older runtime format at startup. For a legacy custom storage.file_path , /path/custom.csv maps to /path/custom/ ; a file named runtime_store.csv maps to its parent. The original file remains as a backup source. Policies now live in the shared files; runtime_metadata.csv retains frequencies and runtime history. Do not delete migration markers to make an old source active again: that can restore deliberately removed entries. If startup reports an invalid legacy header, JSON value, or expiry, repair that source and retry after stopping old workers. See the migration guide for conflict handling and rollback. Node dependency and native startup issues Reproduce the committed dependency tree with npm ci and run the full npm audit . The current source fixes the earlier Jest/Fastify/NestJS advisory chains; an older lockfile can still install vulnerable versions. A deprecation notice or a blocked optional postinstall is not itself an audit result. If native mode cannot find NativeRequestPipeline , inspect the installed aiwaf-wasm package, await the adapter's initialization, and verify that it matches the source API. Keep native profile options separate from legacy constructor options. Node's native event files are distinct from the Python policy schemas and legacy Node stores. Jest's Must use import to load ES Module error can indicate a mismatch between the test dependency tree, Node version, and transform configuration. The repository uses patched NestJS 11 and a targeted cookie transform on Node 22. Retain that configuration when reproducing the source tests. See the tested dependency setup . Use the same absolute data and evidence directories for application workers and CLI trainers. Install the matching native companion before upgrading its host package: Rust before Python, WASM before Node.
